After the closing `}` of Plan S3-D's `message TrackSettle` (411) and before `service ConsensusAdmin {` (413), with one blank line on each side, insert (contract §39 verbatim):

```proto
// RebalanceGroupCmd (Raft tag 38) is both the ConsensusAdmin.RebalanceGroup
// request and the Raft command (spec §6.4). authority_jws is an ES256K JWS by
// a current authority address with purpose "arbiter-rebalance-group-v1" over
// {owner_indexer_id, database_id, expected_generation, add, remove,
// network_fill}, bound to the network id, genesis snapshot id and authority
// epoch. add and remove are sorted, unique and disjoint; network_fill is the
// group's fill after the command.
message RebalanceGroupCmd {
  uint64 owner_indexer_id = 1;
  string database_id = 2;
  uint64 expected_generation = 3;
  repeated string add = 4;
  repeated string remove = 5;
  bool network_fill = 6;
  string authority_jws = 7;
}

// ReselectVerifiersCmd (Raft tag 39) replaces verifiers of one block's set
// (spec §7.4); expected_set is the block's current set, three sorted unique
// ids. Signed by the orchestrator's authority signer, purpose
// "arbiter-reselect-verifiers-v1", context-bound like RebalanceGroupCmd. The
// leader proposes it; there is no RPC. Apply refuses it before the
// reselection switch with "re-selection is refused until the reselection
// switch is on" (plan S3-E1 K67).
message ReselectVerifiersCmd {
  uint64 l3_block_seq = 1;
  repeated string expected_set = 2;
  string authority_jws = 3;
}

// MarkMemberLaggingCmd (Raft tag 42) is both the ConsensusAdmin
// MarkMemberLagging request and the Raft command (spec §9.2); Apply re-checks
// it against committed state. Purpose "arbiter-mark-member-lagging-v1",
// context-bound; observed_entry.indexer_id equals owner_indexer_id.
message MarkMemberLaggingCmd {
  string node_id = 1;
  uint64 owner_indexer_id = 2;
  string database_id = 3;
  TrackFrontier observed_entry = 4;
  string authority_jws = 5;
}

// Stage3SwitchCutover records one stage-3 switch's turn-on: switch_name is the
// Stage3Params field name; epoch is the update's epoch; cutover_block_seq and
// cutover_promotion_seq are the sealed tip (after the update's own seal, for
// placement) and the promotion sequence when it applied.
message Stage3SwitchCutover {
  string switch_name = 1;
  uint64 epoch = 2;
  uint64 cutover_block_seq = 3;
  uint64 cutover_promotion_seq = 4;
}

// Stage3StateView answers ConsensusParamsState.stage3_state: the v21
// activation's epoch, sealed tip and promotion sequence, and every switch
// turned on since, in turn-on order.
message Stage3StateView {
  uint64 activation_epoch = 1;
  uint64 activation_block_seq = 2;
  uint64 activation_promotion_seq = 3;
  repeated Stage3SwitchCutover switches = 4;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 14: Build arbiter-core, arbiter, sentio-node and housegate against the branch**

Local and offline (it reads the local clones' `origin/main` and the Go module cache, `GOPROXY=off`): a scratch copy of each downstream repository with a `replace` of arbiter-proto by this worktree must build and vet, and the tests of every package that imports arbiter-proto or serves the two services must fail only where a mirror sees a new field, before anything is pushed. Run it with the Bash tool's 600000 ms timeout:

```bash
W="$HOME/src/remotesrc/claude/arbiter-proto/multi-source-s3e1"; T57="$HOME/.cache/s3e1-task57"; N=/Users/uranuswch/Dev/projects/sentio-network
export GOWORK=off GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off
rm -rf "$T57/downstream" "$T57/downstream.txt" "$T57/downstream.log" && mkdir -p "$T57/downstream"
for r in arbiter-core arbiter sentio-node housegate; do
  d="$T57/downstream/$r"; mkdir "$d"
  git -C "$N/$r" archive origin/main | tar -x -C "$d"
  printf '\nreplace github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto => %s\n' "$W" >> "$d/go.mod"
  printf '%s %s\n' "$r" "$(git -C "$N/$r" rev-parse --short origin/main)" | tee -a "$T57/downstream.txt"
done
(cd "$T57/downstream/arbiter-core" && go build ./... && go vet ./...) || exit 1
(cd "$T57/downstream/arbiter" && go build ./... && go vet ./...) || exit 1
(cd "$T57/downstream/sentio-node" && go vet ./standalone/ ./storageintegrityadapter/) || exit 1
(cd "$T57/downstream/housegate" && go build ./...) || exit 1
{
  (cd "$T57/downstream/arbiter-core" && go test -count=1 ./conformance/ ./wire/ ./authority/ ./dataplane/ ./snode/)
  (cd "$T57/downstream/arbiter" && go test -count=1 ./server/ ./cmd/arbiter-admin/ ./orchestrator/ ./fsm/)
  (cd "$T57/downstream/sentio-node" && go test -count=1 ./storageintegrityadapter/)
  (cd "$T57/downstream/housegate" && go test -count=1 -vet=off . ./pkg/storageintegrity/ ./pkg/plugins/storageintegrity/)
} > "$T57/downstream.log" 2>&1
grep -E '^(ok|FAIL|--- FAIL)' "$T57/downstream.log" | grep -v '^FAIL$'
python3 -I -c '
import re, sys
new = {"stage3", "stage3_state", "host_indexer_id", "replica_signer", "consent_jws", "weight", "failure_domain", "verify", "replicate", "counts", "shared_rmt", "scoped_keeper_path", "purge_members", "groups", "member_checkpoint_seqs", "group_key", "eligible_ring", "ring_position", "marked_cursor_block", "group_members", "group_fill", "group_databases", "reselections", "reselections_at_latch"}
log = open(sys.argv[1]).read().split("\n")
details = [l.strip() for l in log if re.match(r"^\s+\S+_test\.go:[0-9]+: ", l)]
bad = [l for l in details if not set(re.findall(r"[\x22.]([a-z0-9_]+)", l.split(": ", 1)[1])) & new]
bad += [l.strip() for l in log if re.search(r"\[(build|setup) failed\]$|^panic: ", l)]
```

```go
// TestVerifiersUnavailableIsATerminalRejectWithItsCode pins spec 2026-10-14
// §7.3: the arbiter answers ADMISSION_CODE_VERIFIERS_UNAVAILABLE, with its
// state unchanged, when the eligible ring of the statement's group holds
// fewer than three verifiers, so the outcome is a coded terminal reject. Its
// category removes the prepared parts through the terminal-submit path, and
// its code tells the ingress which client refusal to send.
func TestVerifiersUnavailableIsATerminalRejectWithItsCode(t *testing.T) {
	const reason = "storage-integrity verifiers unavailable for indexer 1: 2 eligible, at least 3 required"
	got := SubmitOutcomeFromSequencedAck(&pb.SequencedAck{Code: pb.AdmissionCode_ADMISSION_CODE_VERIFIERS_UNAVAILABLE, Message: reason})
	if got.Category != OutcomeTerminalReject || got.AdmissionCode != AdmissionCodeVerifiersUnavailable ||
		got.AdmissionCode != "ADMISSION_CODE_VERIFIERS_UNAVAILABLE" || got.Reason != reason {
		t.Fatalf("outcome = %+v", got)
	}
	if !got.Category.RequiresAbort() {
		t.Fatal("a verifiers-unavailable refusal must remove the prepared parts through the terminal-submit path")
	}
	if pb.AdmissionCode_ADMISSION_CODE_VERIFIERS_UNAVAILABLE != 12 {
		t.Fatalf("ADMISSION_CODE_VERIFIERS_UNAVAILABLE = %d, want 12 (plan S3-E1 contract §39)", pb.AdmissionCode_ADMISSION_CODE_VERIFIERS_UNAVAILABLE)
	}
}

// TestCopiesBackpressureIsATerminalRejectWithItsCode pins spec 2026-10-14
// §9.3 and plan S3-E1 K59: with strict_copies on, the arbiter answers
// ADMISSION_CODE_COPIES_BACKPRESSURE, with its state unchanged, while the
// copy floor holds the table's cleanup above its uncleaned-parts bound, so
// the outcome is a coded terminal reject. Its category removes the prepared
// parts through the terminal-submit path, and its code tells the ingress to
// answer back-pressure.
func TestCopiesBackpressureIsATerminalRejectWithItsCode(t *testing.T) {
	const reason = "storage-integrity copy floor: net1.events holds 20001 uncleaned promoted parts (max_uncleaned_parts_per_table 20000) whose cleanup waits for member checkpoints (strict_copies); retry later"
	got := SubmitOutcomeFromSequencedAck(&pb.SequencedAck{Code: pb.AdmissionCode_ADMISSION_CODE_COPIES_BACKPRESSURE, Message: reason})
	if got.Category != OutcomeTerminalReject || got.AdmissionCode != AdmissionCodeCopiesBackpressure ||
		got.AdmissionCode != "ADMISSION_CODE_COPIES_BACKPRESSURE" || got.Reason != reason {
		t.Fatalf("outcome = %+v", got)
	}
	if !got.Category.RequiresAbort() {
		t.Fatal("a copies-backpressure refusal must remove the prepared parts through the terminal-submit path")
	}
	if pb.AdmissionCode_ADMISSION_CODE_COPIES_BACKPRESSURE != 13 {
		t.Fatalf("ADMISSION_CODE_COPIES_BACKPRESSURE = %d, want 13 (plan S3-E1 contract §39)", pb.AdmissionCode_ADMISSION_CODE_COPIES_BACKPRESSURE)
	}
	// Without a message the code names the reason, as for every coded reject.
	if bare := SubmitOutcomeFromSequencedAck(&pb.SequencedAck{Code: pb.AdmissionCode_ADMISSION_CODE_COPIES_BACKPRESSURE}); bare.Reason != AdmissionCodeCopiesBackpressure {
		t.Fatalf("reason without a message = %q, want %q", bare.Reason, AdmissionCodeCopiesBackpressure)
	}
}
```

```go
// TestVerifiersUnavailableMessage pins the exact spec 2026-10-14 §7.3 text
// (plan S3-E1 contract §40); the relay's deferred-lane classifier depends on
// it, and 733 also carries other refusals, so only this exact message may keep
// a session.
func TestVerifiersUnavailableMessage(t *testing.T) {
	if got := VerifiersUnavailableMessage("net1.events"); got != "storage_integrity: the verifiers of table net1.events are not available yet; retry shortly (retryable)" {
		t.Fatalf("VerifiersUnavailableMessage = %q", got)
	}
	if !IsVerifiersUnavailableMessage(VerifiersUnavailableMessage("net1.events")) {
		t.Fatal("IsVerifiersUnavailableMessage rejected its own message")
	}
	if !IsVerifiersUnavailableMessage(VerifiersUnavailableMessage("net1.events") + SeqUnspentSuffix) {
		t.Fatal("IsVerifiersUnavailableMessage must accept the marker suffix")
	}
	for _, msg := range []string{
		"",
		VerifiersUnavailableMessage(""),
		VerifiersUnavailableMessage("net1 events"),
		VerifiersUnavailableMessage("net1.events\t"),
		SourceUnavailableMessage("net1.events"),
		TableActivatingMessage("net1.events"),
		CopiesBackpressureMessage("net1.events"),
		"storage_integrity: the verifiers of table net1.events are not available yet",
		"DB::Exception: " + VerifiersUnavailableMessage("net1.events"),
	} {
		if IsVerifiersUnavailableMessage(msg) {
			t.Fatalf("IsVerifiersUnavailableMessage(%q) = true, want false", msg)
		}
	}
	unavailable := VerifiersUnavailableMessage("net1.events")
	if IsSourceUnavailableMessage(unavailable) || IsTableActivatingMessage(unavailable) || IsTableNoLongerAcceptsWritesMessage(unavailable) ||
		IsIndexerQuarantinedMessage(unavailable) || IsCopiesBackpressureMessage(unavailable) {
		t.Fatal("the verifiers-unavailable refusal must not match the other refusals")
	}
}

// TestCopiesBackpressureMessage pins the exact spec 2026-10-14 §9.3 text (plan
// S3-E1 K59, contract §40). It starts with the back-pressure prefix, so the
// relay's 252 rule keeps the session without a matcher of its own; the
// matcher still tells it apart from local part back-pressure.
func TestCopiesBackpressureMessage(t *testing.T) {
	const want = "storage_integrity: back-pressure: table net1.events waits for its replica copies to catch up; retry later (retryable)"
	if got := CopiesBackpressureMessage("net1.events"); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("CopiesBackpressureMessage = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
	if !IsCopiesBackpressureMessage(CopiesBackpressureMessage("net1.events")) {
		t.Fatal("IsCopiesBackpressureMessage rejected its own message")
	}
	if !IsCopiesBackpressureMessage(CopiesBackpressureMessage("net1.events") + SeqUnspentSuffix) {
		t.Fatal("IsCopiesBackpressureMessage must accept the marker suffix")
	}
	for _, msg := range []string{
		"",
		CopiesBackpressureMessage(""),
		CopiesBackpressureMessage("net1 events"),
		CopiesBackpressureMessage("net1.events\t"),
		"storage_integrity: back-pressure: retry later",
		"storage_integrity: back-pressure: hg_unsafe.net1__events partition p_us has 2400 active parts (soft limit 2400); retry later",
		"storage_integrity: back-pressure: table net1.events waits for its replica copies to catch up",
		VerifiersUnavailableMessage("net1.events"),
		SourceUnavailableMessage("net1.events"),
	} {
		if IsCopiesBackpressureMessage(msg) {
			t.Fatalf("IsCopiesBackpressureMessage(%q) = true, want false", msg)
		}
	}
	backpressure := CopiesBackpressureMessage("net1.events")
	if IsVerifiersUnavailableMessage(backpressure) || IsSourceUnavailableMessage(backpressure) || IsTableActivatingMessage(backpressure) ||
		IsTableNoLongerAcceptsWritesMessage(backpressure) || IsIndexerQuarantinedMessage(backpressure) {
		t.Fatal("the copies back-pressure refusal must not match the other refusals")
	}
}
```

```go
func VerifiersUnavailableMessage(tableID string) string {
```

```go
func TestAdmissionUsesTheSnapshotSchemaNotTheResolver(t *testing.T) {
```

with:

```go
// TestVerifiersUnavailableReachesTheClientAsARetryableRefusal is spec
// 2026-10-14 §7.3: the arbiter refused admission because the eligible ring of
// the table's group holds fewer than three verifiers. The refusal is the
// retryable 733, ends only the query, leaves the coordinate unspent, keeps the
// arbiter's code and reason server-side, is not counted as back-pressure, and
// the terminal-submit path removed the prepared parts.
func TestVerifiersUnavailableReachesTheClientAsARetryableRefusal(t *testing.T) {
	ingress, _, submitter, preparer := newBackpressureIngress(t, &fakePartsPressure{})
	var aborted []sicore.CandidatePart
	preparer.abortFn = func(parts []sicore.CandidatePart) { aborted = parts }
	submitter.outcome = sicore.SubmitOutcome{Category: sicore.OutcomeTerminalReject,
		Reason: "storage-integrity verifiers unavailable for indexer 1: 2 eligible, at least 3 required", AdmissionCode: sicore.AdmissionCodeVerifiersUnavailable}
	before := testutil.ToFloat64(storageIntegrityBackpressureTotal.WithLabelValues("net1__events"))
	err := ingress.ConsumeStorageIntegrityAdmission(context.Background(), bpAdmission())
	var ce *chproto.ClientError
	if !errors.As(err, &ce) || ce.Code != chproto.CodeTableIsBeingRestarted ||
		ce.Message != "storage_integrity: the verifiers of table net1.events are not available yet; retry shortly (retryable)" {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want the retryable verifiers-unavailable refusal", err)
	}
	if !ce.KeepSession || !chproto.KeepsSession(fmt.Errorf("wrapped by the plugin: %w", err)) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %+v, want KeepSession through the plugin's wrapping", ce)
	}
	if !chproto.IsSeqUnspent(err) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want the coordinate marked unspent: the arbiter changed nothing", err)
	}
	if ce.Err == nil || ce.Err.Error() != "arbiter ADMISSION_CODE_VERIFIERS_UNAVAILABLE: storage-integrity verifiers unavailable for indexer 1: 2 eligible, at least 3 required" {
		t.Fatalf("Err = %v, want the arbiter code and reason", ce.Err)
	}
	if preparer.abortCalls != 1 || !slices.Equal(aborted, bpPreparedCandidates()) {
		t.Fatalf("abort calls = %d with %v, want the prepared candidates removed exactly once", preparer.abortCalls, aborted)
	}
	if got := testutil.ToFloat64(storageIntegrityBackpressureTotal.WithLabelValues("net1__events")); got != before {
		t.Fatalf("backpressure counter = %v, want %v: missing verifiers are not back-pressure", got, before)
	}
}

// TestCopiesBackpressureReachesTheClientAsARetryableBackpressure is spec
// 2026-10-14 §9.3 and plan S3-E1 K59: in strict mode the arbiter refused
// admission because the copy floor holds the table's cleanup above its
// uncleaned-parts bound. The refusal is the 252 back-pressure every client
// already retries, counted in storage_integrity_backpressure_total under the
// table's physical name like local back-pressure; it ends only the query,
// leaves the coordinate unspent, keeps the arbiter's code and reason
// server-side, and the terminal-submit path removed the prepared parts.
func TestCopiesBackpressureReachesTheClientAsARetryableBackpressure(t *testing.T) {
	const reason = "storage-integrity copy floor: net1.events holds 20001 uncleaned promoted parts (max_uncleaned_parts_per_table 20000) whose cleanup waits for member checkpoints (strict_copies); retry later"
	ingress, _, submitter, preparer := newBackpressureIngress(t, &fakePartsPressure{})
	var aborted []sicore.CandidatePart
	preparer.abortFn = func(parts []sicore.CandidatePart) { aborted = parts }
	submitter.outcome = sicore.SubmitOutcome{Category: sicore.OutcomeTerminalReject, Reason: reason, AdmissionCode: sicore.AdmissionCodeCopiesBackpressure}
	before := testutil.ToFloat64(storageIntegrityBackpressureTotal.WithLabelValues("net1__events"))
	err := ingress.ConsumeStorageIntegrityAdmission(context.Background(), bpAdmission())
	var ce *chproto.ClientError
	if !errors.As(err, &ce) || ce.Code != chproto.CodeTooManyParts ||
		ce.Message != "storage_integrity: back-pressure: table net1.events waits for its replica copies to catch up; retry later (retryable)" {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want the copies back-pressure refusal", err)
	}
	if !ce.KeepSession || !chproto.KeepsSession(fmt.Errorf("wrapped by the plugin: %w", err)) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %+v, want KeepSession through the plugin's wrapping", ce)
	}
	if !chproto.IsSeqUnspent(err) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want the coordinate marked unspent: the arbiter changed nothing", err)
	}
	if ce.Err == nil || ce.Err.Error() != "arbiter ADMISSION_CODE_COPIES_BACKPRESSURE: "+reason {
		t.Fatalf("Err = %v, want the arbiter code and reason", ce.Err)
	}
	if preparer.abortCalls != 1 || !slices.Equal(aborted, bpPreparedCandidates()) {
		t.Fatalf("abort calls = %d with %v, want the prepared candidates removed exactly once", preparer.abortCalls, aborted)
	}
	if got := testutil.ToFloat64(storageIntegrityBackpressureTotal.WithLabelValues("net1__events")); got != before+1 {
		t.Fatalf("backpressure counter = %v, want %v", got, before+1)
	}
}
```

## Task 59: arbiter-core — pin PROTO_TAG_P5, the stage-3 canonical types, a field-preserving normalizer and the six signing purposes with frozen vectors (S3-E1)

Spec §6.1 (the `verifiers` entry fields and the `stage3` parameter: canonical form and static rules), §6.4 (`RebalanceGroup` and `MemberReady` signing), §7.3 (`VERIFIERS_UNAVAILABLE`), §7.4 (`ReselectVerifiers` signing), §9.1–§9.2 (`MemberCheckpoint`, `MarkMemberLagging`), §9.3 (the strict-mode code), §10.4 (the switch order) and §15 (the arbiter-core line); contract §41 (Task 59's part), clarifications K58 (no hidden default: pool entries keep their v20 form, member entries are explicit) and K63 (six purposes and digest domains, the closed exclusion-reason set). arbiter-core at `CORE_TAG_P4` still pins arbiter-proto `PROTO_TAG_P4`, its `VerifierEntry` has two fields, and `normalizeVerifiers` rebuilds each entry as `{NodeID, Ed25519Pubkey}` (`authority/consensus.go:125` at `cfd4f42`): pinned to `PROTO_TAG_P5` as it is, the normalizer would silently drop every member field before hashing, and a member entry would be signed without its host, signer, consent or flags. This task, the first of Tasks 59–63 on one branch:

- pins `PROTO_TAG_P5` (go.mod and go.sum only) and handles the pin's test fallout: the mirror test that drives the root types, one S3-A every-field test that learns that a promotion outcome's track never carries a `group_key`, and S3-C2's `BlockVerification` every-field test, which stays red until Task 60 (Notes);
- adds the canonical Go types of contract §41 to the root package (`VerifierEntry` fields 3–11 and `IsMember`, `ConsensusParamsUpdate.Stage3`, `stage3.go` with `Stage3Params`, its `Validate`, `FailureDomain`, `Stage3Switches`, `SwitchOn`, the three authority commands, `MemberReadyBody` and the checkpoint types) and admission codes 12 and 13, every new field `omitempty`;
- makes `authority.NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate` copy and check every field (`normalizeStage3`, `cloneVerifierEntry`, every `stage3:` and `verifiers:` refusal of contract §41, verbatim);
- adds the six purposes with their hash, sign and verify functions (`authority/stage3.go`) and their frozen vectors (`authority/authoritytest/stage3.go`, `authority/stage3_golden_test.go`), computed outside Go and rechecked outside Go with public data only;
- adds the canonical mirror and admission-code conformance tests (`conformance/stage3_wire_test.go`).

It changes no consensus byte: a pool-only update hashes exactly as before (`authoritytest.ActivationUpdateHash` and `TestConsensusParamsUpdateHashIsFrozen` pass unedited), and nothing here proposes, decodes or applies a stage-3 command (Task 60 adds the wire, S3-E2–E4 the FSM).

Notes:
- **Base.** arbiter-core at `CORE_TAG_P4` (Plan S3-D Task 50), read from the ledger; it pins arbiter-proto `PROTO_TAG_P4` (S3-D contract §34). The anchors below are those of `origin/main` `cfd4f42` (S3-A merged as arbiter-core#50). Of this task's files the releases in between change only these: Plan S3-D Task 50 appends `SettleTrackCommand` at the end of `consensus.go` (after `ReleaseIndexerCommand.Validate`, below every hunk here) and adds `authority/settle.go` (`SettleTrackPurpose`, which `TestStage3TokensDoNotCrossPurposes` lists) with its tests; Plan S3-C2 Task 29 adds `wire/block_verification.go` and `wire/block_verification_test.go`; gazelle adds those files to the same `BUILD.bazel` lists this task extends. Plans S3-C1 and S3-C4 touch none of this task's files. Every hunk anchors on text those changes leave as it is (the hunk rule), and Step 1 checks it.
- **The pin's test fallout (measured; contract issue recorded in Appendix B).** `PROTO_TAG_P5` appends fields to messages that three existing every-field tests walk, so after the pin `bazel test` fails in exactly two targets and nothing fails to build: `//conformance:conformance_test` `TestArbiterMirrorsMatchProto` (`ConsensusParamsUpdate: proto field "stage3" has no Go mirror json tag` and nine `VerifierEntry` lines for fields 3–11) is this task's failing test for the root types and passes, unedited, once they exist (contract §41); `//wire:wire_test` `TestPromotionOutcomesConvertersCopyEveryField` (S3-A Task 4, `arbiter.L3BlockTrack.group_key is unset`) and S3-C2's `TestBlockVerificationFromPBReadsEveryField` (`arbiter.BlockVerification.eligible_ring has no case: BlockVerification and this test must carry it`). The first wire test is not a gap: `wire.PromotionOutcome` names its promotion's track by the owner only (`TrackIndexerID`), the arbiter builds an outcome's track as `{IndexerID}` alone (arbiter `fsm/reads_promotions.go:90`, `server/safestate_stage3.go:125`), and a block's `group_key` is read through `GetBlockVerification`; Step 3 exempts that one proto field in the test with that reason (`wire/stage3_reads_test.go` is not a frozen file; S3-A froze only the arbiter-proto ledgers and arbiter-core's `conformance/stage3_reads_test.go`, which is not edited). The second is S3-C2's own design ("Plan S3-E1 (fields 14–22) extends the Go type and the cases together"), and contract §41 places `wire.BlockVerification`'s nine new fields in Task 60, so it stays red from this task's pin until Task 60 extends the type and the test's cases. Tasks 59–63 share one branch whose single PR opens in Task 63, so no red commit reaches `main`; every step below names this failure, and any other failure is a stop.
- **Canonical forms (K58).** Every field added to a hashed type is `omitempty` (`ConsensusParamsUpdate.Stage3` a nil pointer, `VerifierEntry.HostIndexerID` a `*uint64` because indexer 0 is a valid host), so an update without `stage3` and a pool entry encode exactly as under `CORE_TAG_P4`: `TestPoolVerifierEntryKeepsItsV20CanonicalForm` checks the existing `ActivationUpdateHash` and the pool entries' two-member JSON. `Stage3Params` itself has no `omitempty` except on `indexer_failure_domains` (contract §41): once present it is explicit. The normalizer refuses a member field on a pool entry, so no pool entry ever hashes differently; on a member entry an unset bool or zero weight is omitted from the canonical JSON and means false or 0 (never a default; `arbiter-admin` supplies the spec's "true" and "1" in S3-E2 Task 65).
- **The normalizer.** `NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate` keeps its existing checks and order and adds, after `normalizeSIIndexers`: `normalizeStage3` (sorts a copy of the failure domains by indexer id, nil when empty; `Stage3Params.Validate`; `stage3 requires tracks_enabled in the same update`; every domain names an indexer of the normalized `si_indexers`; with the placement switch every indexer has a domain), then `normalizeVerifiers(in, siIndexers, stage3)`, which copies every field (`cloneVerifierEntry`: the key bytes and the host pointer detached from the caller's, `ReplicaSigner` lowercased), refuses the per-entry rules, keeps the sort and the duplicate node-id and key refusals, refuses a shared replica signer, and checks every member against the update's `si_indexers` and `stage3`. Every refusal is contract §41's text behind the existing `consensus params update: ` prefix. Consent verification, "node id unused by every registered node", the per-group floor and the one-way rules stay with the FSM (S3-E2 Task 64).
- **Purposes (K63).** The three authority commands follow the quarantine precedent (`signWithContextPurpose`, `verifyExactContext` with labels `rebalance group`, `reselect verifiers`, `mark member lagging`; `Verify…` reads no clock for Apply and restore, `Authorize…` adds the token age for the RPCs). The consent follows the SNode enrolment (`signPayload`, `verifySignedBy`; network and genesis inside the statement; its replica signer hashed lowercase, the form the normalizer gives the entry, so a checksummed address names the same statement). MemberReady is the verifier-message convention (lowercase hex `ed25519.Sign(priv, []byte(hash))`) under its own domain; the checkpoint is an ES256K token of the entry's `replica_signer`. Both member messages hash the preimage `{"context": MessageContext, "body": <body>}`. Lists are validated and never sorted by a hash (the `ReleaseIndexerHash` precedent), and an empty `Add`, `Remove` or `Excluded` hashes as an absent one. `TestStage3TokensDoNotCrossPurposes` signs every stage-3 hash under every other stage-3 and earlier purpose (`PromotionPurpose`, `ConsensusParamsUpdatePurpose`, `EvictNodePurpose`, `QuarantineIndexerPurpose`, `ReleaseIndexerPurpose`, S3-D's `SettleTrackPurpose`, `SNodeEnrollmentPurpose`, `SNodeMessagePurpose`, `ArtifactDispositionAdminPurpose`, `QueryProfileActivationPurpose`, `SnapshotQueryAbortPurpose`), with and without a context, and checks each refusal.
- **Vectors.** Fixture identities and values are contract §41's. `Stage3Update()` also enrols indexer 1 (`SIIndexerEntry1(6_000_000)`, `MaxWriters` 2): contract §41 asks for failure domains of indexers 0 and 1, and the normalizer refuses a domain of an indexer the update does not enrol (`stage3: indexer_failure_domains names indexer 1, which has no si_indexers entry`); member-b's host is indexer 1 as well (Appendix B). Every hash was computed outside Go as `sha256("housegate-replay-mvp-v0:" + domain + "\x00" + json)` with `shasum -a 256` over preimages written by hand from the field order (the method reproduces the existing `ActivationUpdateHash`), every ES256K token as `cast keccak` of the signing input then `cast wallet sign --no-hash` with the fixture key, and the MemberReady signature with OpenSSL's ed25519 over the hash string and the fixture seed (2026-10-16, in a scratch directory; the throwaway fixture keys are those of `authoritytest`). Go reproduces each byte for byte (ES256K through go-ethereum's `crypto.Sign` is deterministic, RFC 6979). Step 22 rechecks every constant outside Go with public data only (preimages, addresses, the member-b public key), so no key or seed is on argv. `Stage3MemberUpdateHash` (the update listing member-b) is one constant beyond contract §41's list: it freezes a member entry's canonical form, every field in proto order (Appendix B). They are consensus constants once committed: never regenerate them.

```go
package arbiter

import (

	"testing"

// validStage3Params is a complete parameter with every switch off, the shape
// of the v21 activation (plan S3-E1 K58: every field explicit).
func validStage3Params() Stage3Params {
	return Stage3Params{GroupSize: 3, NetworkFillDefault: true, MinSafeCopies: 1,
		IndexerFailureDomains: []IndexerFailureDomain{{IndexerID: 0, FailureDomain: "node:a"}, {IndexerID: 1, FailureDomain: "node:b"}},
		MaxLagPublications:    4, LagLow: 2, EvidenceTimeoutL2Blocks: 30, MaxUncleanedPartsPerPartition: 2400, MaxUncleanedPartsPerTable: 20000}
}

// withSwitches returns p with exactly the named switches on.
func withSwitches(p Stage3Params, names ...string) Stage3Params {
	v := reflect.ValueOf(&p).Elem()
	for _, name := range names {
		for i := 0; i < v.NumField(); i++ {
			if strings.Split(v.Type().Field(i).Tag.Get("json"), ",")[0] == name {
				v.Field(i).SetBool(true)
			}
		}
	}
	return p
}

		"lag_low equal":      {func(p *Stage3Params) { p.LagLow = 4 }, "stage3: lag_low must satisfy 1 <= lag_low < max_lag_publications, got lag_low 4 and max_lag_publications 4"},
		"no max lag":         {func(p *Stage3Params) { p.MaxLagPublications, p.LagLow = 0, 0 }, "stage3: lag_low must satisfy 1 <= lag_low < max_lag_publications, got lag_low 0 and max_lag_publications 0"},

		"strict without drain": {func(p *Stage3Params) { *p = withSwitches(*p, Stage3Switches[:6]...); p.StrictCopies = true }, "stage3: min_safe_copies above 1 and strict_copies require the checkpoints and narrowed_drain switches"},

// TestStage3SwitchesArePrefixes: the switches are the last seven fields of
// Stage3Params in §10.4 order, SwitchOn reads exactly its own field, every
// prefix of the order validates, and a switch whose earlier switch is off is
// refused naming the first earlier one that is off.
func TestStage3SwitchesArePrefixes(t *testing.T) {
	want := []string{"purge", "eviction_voiding", "owner_aware_selection", "placement", "reselection", "checkpoints", "narrowed_drain"}
	if !slices.Equal(Stage3Switches, want) {
		t.Fatalf("Stage3Switches = %v, want %v", Stage3Switches, want)
	}
	rt := reflect.TypeOf(Stage3Params{})
	for i, name := range Stage3Switches {
		f := rt.Field(rt.NumField() - len(Stage3Switches) + i)
		if f.Type.Kind() != reflect.Bool || strings.Split(f.Tag.Get("json"), ",")[0] != name {
			t.Fatalf("field %s (%s) is not switch %s", f.Name, f.Tag.Get("json"), name)
		}
		one := withSwitches(Stage3Params{}, name)
		for _, other := range Stage3Switches {
			if one.SwitchOn(other) != (other == name) {
				t.Fatalf("with only %s on, SwitchOn(%s) = %v", name, other, one.SwitchOn(other))
			}
		}
	}
	if (withSwitches(Stage3Params{}, Stage3Switches...)).SwitchOn("strict_copies") {
		t.Fatal("SwitchOn answered true for a name that is not a switch")
	}
	for n := 0; n <= len(Stage3Switches); n++ {
		if err := withSwitches(validStage3Params(), Stage3Switches[:n]...).Validate(); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("prefix %v: %v", Stage3Switches[:n], err)
		}
	}
	for i := range Stage3Switches {
		for j := 0; j < i; j++ {
			on := slices.Concat(Stage3Switches[:j], Stage3Switches[j+1:i+1])
			err := withSwitches(validStage3Params(), on...).Validate()
			if wantErr := "stage3: switch " + Stage3Switches[j+1] + " requires " + Stage3Switches[j]; err == nil || err.Error() != wantErr {
				t.Fatalf("%v on without %s: Validate = %v, want %q", on, Stage3Switches[j], err, wantErr)
			}
		}
	}
}

// TestStage3FailureDomainLookupAndIsMember: FailureDomain finds a listed
// indexer (indexer 0 included) and nothing else, and an entry is a member
// exactly when it names a host, indexer 0 included.
func TestStage3FailureDomainLookupAndIsMember(t *testing.T) {
	p := validStage3Params()
	if d, ok := p.FailureDomain(0); !ok || d != "node:a" {
		t.Fatalf("FailureDomain(0) = %q, %v", d, ok)
	}
	if d, ok := p.FailureDomain(1); !ok || d != "node:b" {
		t.Fatalf("FailureDomain(1) = %q, %v", d, ok)
	}
	if d, ok := p.FailureDomain(2); ok || d != "" {
		t.Fatalf("FailureDomain(2) = %q, %v; want none", d, ok)
	}
	zero := uint64(0)
	if (VerifierEntry{NodeID: "verifier-1"}).IsMember() || !(VerifierEntry{NodeID: "member-a", HostIndexerID: &zero}).IsMember() {
		t.Fatal("IsMember must be true exactly when host_indexer_id is set, indexer 0 included")
	}
}

// TestStage3FieldsAreOmittedWhenUnset: an update without stage3 and a pool
// entry encode exactly as before the stage-3 fields existed, so every earlier
// digest is unchanged; a member hosted by indexer 0 keeps its host.
func TestStage3FieldsAreOmittedWhenUnset(t *testing.T) {
	b, err := json.Marshal(ConsensusParamsUpdate{NetworkID: "n", Verifiers: []VerifierEntry{{NodeID: "verifier-1", Ed25519Pubkey: []byte{1}}}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(string(b), `"verifiers":[{"node_id":"verifier-1","ed25519_pubkey":"AQ=="}]`) || strings.Contains(string(b), "stage3") {
		t.Fatalf("pool-only update JSON = %s", b)
	}
	zero := uint64(0)
	b, err = json.Marshal(VerifierEntry{NodeID: "member-a", HostIndexerID: &zero})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if string(b) != `{"node_id":"member-a","ed25519_pubkey":null,"host_indexer_id":0}` {
		t.Fatalf("member hosted by indexer 0 = %s", b)
	}
}
```

Create `conformance/stage3_wire_test.go`:

```go
package conformance

import (
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/proto"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/reflect/protoreflect"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
)

// assertMirrorOrder pins that a canonical stage-3 mirror lists its fields in
// proto field-number order (request-only fields skipped), so its canonical
// JSON, and every digest over it, follows the wire order (plan S3-E1 contract
// §41). assertMirror pins the names; this pins the order.
func assertMirrorOrder(t *testing.T, goValue any, msg proto.Message, requestOnly ...string) {
	t.Helper()
	rt := reflect.TypeOf(goValue)
	var goNames []string
	for i := 0; i < rt.NumField(); i++ {
		goNames = append(goNames, strings.Split(rt.Field(i).Tag.Get("json"), ",")[0])
	}
	var protoNames []string
	fields := msg.ProtoReflect().Descriptor().Fields()
	for i := 0; i < fields.Len(); i++ {
		if name := string(fields.Get(i).Name()); !slices.Contains(requestOnly, name) {
			protoNames = append(protoNames, name)
		}
	}
	if !slices.Equal(goNames, protoNames) {
		t.Errorf("%s fields %v are not in the proto order %v", rt.Name(), goNames, protoNames)
	}
}

// TestStage3CanonicalMirrorsMatchProto pins every stage-3 canonical type of
// contract §41 to its pb message by name and order. The signatures beside
// the signed bodies (authority_jws, ed25519_signature) are request-only. The
// closed exclusion-reason set is the pb enum without UNSPECIFIED, and the
// switch names are the last seven pb.Stage3Params fields in order.
func TestStage3CanonicalMirrorsMatchProto(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		goValue     any
		msg         proto.Message
		requestOnly []string
	}{
		{arbiter.Stage3Params{}, &pb.Stage3Params{}, nil},
		{arbiter.IndexerFailureDomain{}, &pb.IndexerFailureDomain{}, nil},
		{arbiter.VerifierEntry{}, &pb.VerifierEntry{}, nil},
		{arbiter.RebalanceGroupCommand{}, &pb.RebalanceGroupCmd{}, []string{"authority_jws"}},
		{arbiter.ReselectVerifiersCommand{}, &pb.ReselectVerifiersCmd{}, []string{"authority_jws"}},
		{arbiter.MarkMemberLaggingCommand{}, &pb.MarkMemberLaggingCmd{}, []string{"authority_jws"}},
		{arbiter.MemberReadyBody{}, &pb.MemberReadyCmd{}, []string{"ed25519_signature"}},
		{arbiter.MemberCheckpoint{}, &pb.MemberCheckpoint{}, nil},
		{arbiter.CheckpointGroup{}, &pb.CheckpointGroup{}, nil},
		{arbiter.ExcludedTable{}, &pb.ExcludedTable{}, nil},
	} {
		assertMirror(t, tc.goValue, tc.msg, tc.requestOnly...)
		assertMirrorOrder(t, tc.goValue, tc.msg, tc.requestOnly...)
	}
	values := pb.CheckpointExclusionReason(0).Descriptor().Values()
	var reasons []arbiter.CheckpointExclusionReason
	for i := 0; i < values.Len(); i++ {
		if n := values.Get(i).Number(); n != 0 {
			reasons = append(reasons, arbiter.CheckpointExclusionReason(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimPrefix(string(values.Get(i).Name()), "CHECKPOINT_EXCLUSION_REASON_"))))
		}
	}
	if want := []arbiter.CheckpointExclusionReason{arbiter.ExclusionNotInstalled, arbiter.ExclusionDiverged, arbiter.ExclusionForeign,
		arbiter.ExclusionDiskThreshold, arbiter.ExclusionAuditPending, arbiter.ExclusionRetiring}; !slices.Equal(reasons, want) {
		t.Fatalf("exclusion reasons %v, want the pb enum's %v", want, reasons)
	}
	fields := (&pb.Stage3Params{}).ProtoReflect().Descriptor().Fields()
	for i, name := range arbiter.Stage3Switches {
		f := fields.ByNumber(protoreflect.FieldNumber(12 + i))
		if f == nil || string(f.Name()) != name || f.Kind() != protoreflect.BoolKind {
			t.Fatalf("switch %s is not pb.Stage3Params field %d: %v", name, 12+i, f)
		}
	}
	if fields.Len() != 11+len(arbiter.Stage3Switches) {
		t.Fatalf("pb.Stage3Params has %d fields, want %d", fields.Len(), 11+len(arbiter.Stage3Switches))
	}
}

// TestStage3AdmissionCodesMatchProto pins the two stage-3 admission codes
// (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §7.3, §9.3; plan S3-E1 K59).
func TestStage3AdmissionCodesMatchProto(t *testing.T) {
	if int32(arbiter.AdmissionCodeVerifiersUnavailable) != int32(pb.AdmissionCode_ADMISSION_CODE_VERIFIERS_UNAVAILABLE) || arbiter.AdmissionCodeVerifiersUnavailable != 12 ||
		int32(arbiter.AdmissionCodeCopiesBackpressure) != int32(pb.AdmissionCode_ADMISSION_CODE_COPIES_BACKPRESSURE) || arbiter.AdmissionCodeCopiesBackpressure != 13 {
		t.Fatal("the stage-3 AdmissionCode constants drifted from the pb enum numbers 12 and 13")
	}
}
```

with:

```go
// VerifierEntry lists one verifier that may register (spec D7): its node id
// and the ed25519 key that signs its registration, activation, purge reports
// and evidence. An entry without HostIndexerID is a network-pool verifier and
// sets nothing else, so its canonical form is the one every earlier digest
// hashed. An entry with HostIndexerID is a stage-3 member (housegate spec
// 2026-10-14 §6.1) hosted by that SI indexer (a pointer: indexer 0 is a valid
// host) and states every other field explicitly, with no absent-means-default
// (plan S3-E1 K58): ReplicaSigner (lowercase 0x + 40 hex) signs its
// checkpoints, ConsentJWS is the host signer's ES256K consent (purpose
// arbiter-group-member-v1, verified by the FSM), Weight is 1-64, and
// FailureDomain equals the stage3 parameter's domain of the host. Every
// stage-3 field is omitempty, so a pool entry hashes as it always did.
type VerifierEntry struct {
	NodeID        string  `json:"node_id"`
	Ed25519Pubkey []byte  `json:"ed25519_pubkey"`
	HostIndexerID *uint64 `json:"host_indexer_id,omitempty"`
	ReplicaSigner string  `json:"replica_signer,omitempty"`
	ConsentJWS    string  `json:"consent_jws,omitempty"`
	Weight        uint32  `json:"weight,omitempty"`
	FailureDomain string  `json:"failure_domain,omitempty"`
	Verify        bool    `json:"verify,omitempty"`
	Replicate     bool    `json:"replicate,omitempty"`
```

```go
package arbiter

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"
)

// IndexerFailureDomain names one enrolled SI indexer's failure domain
// (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §6.1, §9.3); equal strings are one domain.
type IndexerFailureDomain struct {
	IndexerID     uint64 `json:"indexer_id"`
	FailureDomain string `json:"failure_domain"`
}

// Stage3Params is the canonical stage-3 parameter (spec §6.1, §10.4), the
// mirror of pb.Stage3Params. Every field is explicit: there is no
// absent-means-default (plan S3-E1 K58), and only IndexerFailureDomains is
// omitted when empty. The switches (Purge through NarrowedDrain, in the order
// of Stage3Switches) and StrictCopies are one-way, and MinSafeCopies and
// GroupSize never decrease; those rules compare two parameters and are the
// FSM's. Validate checks the rules one parameter carries by itself.
type Stage3Params struct {
	GroupSize                     uint32                 `json:"group_size"`
	NetworkFillDefault            bool                   `json:"network_fill_default"`
	MinSafeCopies                 uint32                 `json:"min_safe_copies"`
	StrictCopies                  bool                   `json:"strict_copies"`
	IndexerFailureDomains         []IndexerFailureDomain `json:"indexer_failure_domains,omitempty"`
	MaxLagPublications            uint32                 `json:"max_lag_publications"`
	LagLow                        uint32                 `json:"lag_low"`
	EvidenceTimeoutL2Blocks       uint64                 `json:"evidence_timeout_l2_blocks"`
	MaxUncleanedPartsPerPartition uint32                 `json:"max_uncleaned_parts_per_partition"`
	MaxUncleanedPartsPerTable     uint32                 `json:"max_uncleaned_parts_per_table"`
	ExcludeQuarantinedHosts       bool                   `json:"exclude_quarantined_hosts"`
	Purge                         bool                   `json:"purge"`
	EvictionVoiding               bool                   `json:"eviction_voiding"`
	OwnerAwareSelection           bool                   `json:"owner_aware_selection"`
	Placement                     bool                   `json:"placement"`
	Reselection                   bool                   `json:"reselection"`
	Checkpoints                   bool                   `json:"checkpoints"`
	NarrowedDrain                 bool                   `json:"narrowed_drain"`
}

// Stage3Switches lists the switch names in §10.4 order: "purge", "eviction_voiding",
// "owner_aware_selection", "placement", "reselection", "checkpoints", "narrowed_drain".
// Each is the JSON name of a Stage3Params field; each switch requires every
// earlier one. Read-only.
var Stage3Switches = []string{"purge", "eviction_voiding", "owner_aware_selection", "placement", "reselection", "checkpoints", "narrowed_drain"}

// SwitchOn reports whether the named switch is on; a name that is not in
// Stage3Switches is never on.
func (p Stage3Params) SwitchOn(name string) bool {
	switch name {
	case "purge":
		return p.Purge
	case "eviction_voiding":
		return p.EvictionVoiding
	case "owner_aware_selection":
		return p.OwnerAwareSelection
	case "placement":
		return p.Placement
	case "reselection":
		return p.Reselection
	case "checkpoints":
		return p.Checkpoints
	case "narrowed_drain":
		return p.NarrowedDrain
	}
	return false
}

// FailureDomain returns the failure domain IndexerFailureDomains names for
// indexerID, and whether it names one.
func (p Stage3Params) FailureDomain(indexerID uint64) (string, bool) {
	for _, d := range p.IndexerFailureDomains {
		if d.IndexerID == indexerID {
			return d.FailureDomain, true
		}
	}
	return "", false
}

// Validate checks the rules a single stage-3 parameter carries (plan S3-E1
// contract §41): the bounds, the domain list (sorted by indexer id without
// duplicates; authority.NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate sorts it first), the
// switch prefix rule, and the static form of the copy-floor rule of plan S3-E2
// K69. Whether the domains name exactly the enrolled indexers is checked
// against the update's si_indexers by the normalizer.
func (p Stage3Params) Validate() error {
	switch {
	case p.GroupSize < 1:
		return fmt.Errorf("stage3: group_size must be at least 1")
	case p.MinSafeCopies < 1:
		return fmt.Errorf("stage3: min_safe_copies must be at least 1")
	case p.LagLow < 1 || p.LagLow >= p.MaxLagPublications:
		return fmt.Errorf("stage3: lag_low must satisfy 1 <= lag_low < max_lag_publications, got lag_low %d and max_lag_publications %d", p.LagLow, p.MaxLagPublications)
	case p.EvidenceTimeoutL2Blocks < 1:
		return fmt.Errorf("stage3: evidence_timeout_l2_blocks must be at least 1")
	case p.MaxUncleanedPartsPerPartition < 1 || p.MaxUncleanedPartsPerTable < 1:
		return fmt.Errorf("stage3: max_uncleaned_parts_per_partition and max_uncleaned_parts_per_table must be at least 1")
	}
	for i, d := range p.IndexerFailureDomains {
		if !validNodeID(d.FailureDomain) {
			return fmt.Errorf("stage3: indexer_failure_domains: indexer %d: failure_domain must be non-empty and free of whitespace and control characters", d.IndexerID)
		}
		if i > 0 && p.IndexerFailureDomains[i-1].IndexerID >= d.IndexerID {
			return fmt.Errorf("stage3: indexer_failure_domains must be sorted by indexer_id without duplicates")
		}
	}
	for i, name := range Stage3Switches {
		if !p.SwitchOn(name) {
			continue
		}
		for _, earlier := range Stage3Switches[:i] {
			if !p.SwitchOn(earlier) {
				return fmt.Errorf("stage3: switch %s requires %s", name, earlier)
			}
		}
	}
	if (p.MinSafeCopies > 1 || p.StrictCopies) && !(p.Checkpoints && p.NarrowedDrain) {
		return fmt.Errorf("stage3: min_safe_copies above 1 and strict_copies require the checkpoints and narrowed_drain switches")
	}
	return nil
}

// RebalanceGroupCommand is the canonical signing form of an authority-signed
// RebalanceGroup (spec §6.4); its wire form is pb.RebalanceGroupCmd minus
// authority_jws. ExpectedGeneration is a compare-and-swap on the group's
// generation; Add and Remove are sorted, unique and disjoint, nil (omitted)
// when empty; NetworkFill is the group's fill after the command.
type RebalanceGroupCommand struct {
	OwnerIndexerID     uint64   `json:"owner_indexer_id"`
	DatabaseID         string   `json:"database_id"`
	ExpectedGeneration uint64   `json:"expected_generation"`
	Add                []string `json:"add,omitempty"`
	Remove             []string `json:"remove,omitempty"`
	NetworkFill        bool     `json:"network_fill"`
}

// ReselectVerifiersCommand is the canonical signing form of the
// orchestrator's ReselectVerifiers (spec §7.4); its wire form is
// pb.ReselectVerifiersCmd minus authority_jws. ExpectedSet is the block's
// current verifier set: three sorted, unique node ids.
type ReselectVerifiersCommand struct {
	L3BlockSeq  uint64   `json:"l3_block_seq"`
	ExpectedSet []string `json:"expected_set"`
}

// MarkMemberLaggingCommand is the canonical signing form of an
// authority-signed MarkMemberLagging (spec §9.2); its wire form is
// pb.MarkMemberLaggingCmd minus authority_jws. ObservedEntry.IndexerID equals
// OwnerIndexerID.
type MarkMemberLaggingCommand struct {
	NodeID         string               `json:"node_id"`
	OwnerIndexerID uint64               `json:"owner_indexer_id"`
	DatabaseID     string               `json:"database_id"`
	ObservedEntry  replay.TrackFrontier `json:"observed_entry"`
}

// MemberReadyBody is what a member's ed25519 MemberReady signature covers
// (spec §6.4), with the network context; its wire form is pb.MemberReadyCmd
// minus ed25519_signature.
type MemberReadyBody struct {
	NodeID         string `json:"node_id"`
	OwnerIndexerID uint64 `json:"owner_indexer_id"`
	DatabaseID     string `json:"database_id"`
	Generation     uint64 `json:"generation"`
}

// CheckpointExclusionReason is why a checkpoint excludes a table (plan S3-E1
// K63): the closed set below, the lowercase names of
// pb.CheckpointExclusionReason without its prefix. Any other value, the empty
// one included, is refused.
type CheckpointExclusionReason string

const (
	ExclusionNotInstalled  CheckpointExclusionReason = "not_installed"
	ExclusionDiverged      CheckpointExclusionReason = "diverged"
	ExclusionForeign       CheckpointExclusionReason = "foreign"
	ExclusionDiskThreshold CheckpointExclusionReason = "disk_threshold"
	ExclusionAuditPending  CheckpointExclusionReason = "audit_pending"
	ExclusionRetiring      CheckpointExclusionReason = "retiring"
)

// ExcludedTable is one table a checkpoint group does not speak for.
type ExcludedTable struct {
	TableID string                    `json:"table_id"`
	Reason  CheckpointExclusionReason `json:"reason"`
}

// CheckpointGroup is one group a checkpoint speaks for; Excluded is sorted by
// table id without duplicates, nil (omitted) when empty.
type CheckpointGroup struct {
	DatabaseID      string          `json:"database_id"`
	GroupGeneration uint64          `json:"group_generation"`
	Excluded        []ExcludedTable `json:"excluded,omitempty"`
}

// MemberCheckpoint is the canonical signing form of a replicate member's
// checkpoint (spec §9.1): its copies of the listed groups' tables equal the
// manifest SnapshotID at Entry = track_frontiers[OwnerIndexerID].
// CheckpointSeq strictly increases per (member, owner); Groups is sorted by
// database id without duplicates. The member's replica_signer signs it with
// the network context; its wire form is pb.MemberCheckpoint.
type MemberCheckpoint struct {
	NodeID         string               `json:"node_id"`
	OwnerIndexerID uint64               `json:"owner_indexer_id"`
	CheckpointSeq  uint64               `json:"checkpoint_seq"`
	Groups         []CheckpointGroup    `json:"groups"`
	SnapshotID     string               `json:"snapshot_id"`
	Entry          replay.TrackFrontier `json:"entry"`
}
```

```go
package authority

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"testing"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
)

// testMemberEntry is member-b hosted by indexer 1 with every field set; its
// replica signer is mixed-case, which the normalizer lowercases.
func testMemberEntry() arbiter.VerifierEntry {
	host := uint64(1)
	return arbiter.VerifierEntry{NodeID: "member-b", Ed25519Pubkey: bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x0b}, 32), HostIndexerID: &host,
		ReplicaSigner: "0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000B2", ConsentJWS: "h.p.s", Weight: 2, FailureDomain: "node:b",
		Verify: true, Replicate: true, Counts: true, SharedRMT: true}
}

// stage3TestUpdate is signedClaimsTestUpdate (indexers 0 and 1, verifiers
// 1-3) with the tracks activation, a stage-3 parameter whose failure domains
// are listed out of order, and member-b.
func stage3TestUpdate() arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate {
	u := signedClaimsTestUpdate()
	u.TracksEnabled = true
	u.Stage3 = &arbiter.Stage3Params{GroupSize: 3, NetworkFillDefault: true, MinSafeCopies: 1,
		IndexerFailureDomains: []arbiter.IndexerFailureDomain{{IndexerID: 1, FailureDomain: "node:b"}, {IndexerID: 0, FailureDomain: "node:a"}},
		MaxLagPublications:    4, LagLow: 2, EvidenceTimeoutL2Blocks: 30, MaxUncleanedPartsPerPartition: 2400, MaxUncleanedPartsPerTable: 20000}
	u.Verifiers = append(u.Verifiers, testMemberEntry())
	return u
}

// memberOf returns the normalized entry of nodeID.
func memberOf(t *testing.T, u arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate, nodeID string) arbiter.VerifierEntry {
	t.Helper()
	for _, v := range u.Verifiers {
		if v.NodeID == nodeID {
			return v
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("no verifiers entry %s in %+v", nodeID, u.Verifiers)
	return arbiter.VerifierEntry{}
}

// TestVerifierEntryEveryFieldSurvivesNormalize: a member entry with every
// field set comes out of the normalizer equal (its replica signer
// lowercased), detached from the caller's key and host, and with one canonical
// JSON member per field, so the update hash binds every field. A field added
// to VerifierEntry fails here until the fixture sets it (the precedent of
// arbiter fsm/signed_messages_test.go TestSameRegistrationCoversEveryField).
func TestVerifierEntryEveryFieldSurvivesNormalize(t *testing.T) {
	in := testMemberEntry()
	rv := reflect.ValueOf(in)
	for i := 0; i < rv.NumField(); i++ {
		if rv.Field(i).IsZero() {
			t.Fatalf("testMemberEntry leaves VerifierEntry.%s unset: set it so this test covers it", rv.Type().Field(i).Name)
		}
	}
	u := stage3TestUpdate()
	got, err := NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate(u)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := testMemberEntry()
	want.ReplicaSigner = "0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000b2"
	out := memberOf(t, got, "member-b")
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(out, want) {
		t.Fatalf("normalized entry\n got %+v\nwant %+v", out, want)
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var members map[string]json.RawMessage
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &members); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(members) != rv.NumField() {
		t.Fatalf("canonical JSON %s has %d members, VerifierEntry has %d fields", b, len(members), rv.NumField())
	}
	*out.HostIndexerID, out.Ed25519Pubkey[0] = 7, 0xff
	if caller := u.Verifiers[3]; *caller.HostIndexerID != 1 || caller.Ed25519Pubkey[0] != 0x0b {
		t.Fatal("the normalized entry aliases the caller's host_indexer_id or ed25519_pubkey")
	}
	base, err := ConsensusParamsUpdateHash(stage3TestUpdate())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	other := stage3TestUpdate()
	other.Verifiers[3].Weight = 3
	if h, err := ConsensusParamsUpdateHash(other); err != nil || h == base {
		t.Fatalf("weight is not bound by the update hash: %s, %v", h, err)
	}
}

// TestPoolVerifierEntryRefusesMemberFields: an entry without host_indexer_id
// carries none of the member fields, before and after the stage-3 activation,
// so its bytes and canonical form stay those of every earlier epoch.
func TestPoolVerifierEntryRefusesMemberFields(t *testing.T) {
	const want = "consensus params update: verifiers: verifier-1: an entry without host_indexer_id carries no replica_signer, consent_jws, weight, failure_domain or member flags"
	for name, set := range map[string]func(*arbiter.VerifierEntry){
		"replica_signer": func(e *arbiter.VerifierEntry) { e.ReplicaSigner = "0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000b2" },
		"consent_jws":    func(e *arbiter.VerifierEntry) { e.ConsentJWS = "h.p.s" },
		"weight":         func(e *arbiter.VerifierEntry) { e.Weight = 1 },
		"failure_domain": func(e *arbiter.VerifierEntry) { e.FailureDomain = "node:a" },
		"verify":         func(e *arbiter.VerifierEntry) { e.Verify = true },
		"replicate":      func(e *arbiter.VerifierEntry) { e.Replicate = true },
		"counts":         func(e *arbiter.VerifierEntry) { e.Counts = true },
		"shared_rmt":     func(e *arbiter.VerifierEntry) { e.SharedRMT = true },
	} {
		for update, u := range map[string]arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate{"signed claims": signedClaimsTestUpdate(), "stage3": stage3TestUpdate()} {
			t.Run(name+" in a "+update+" update", func(t *testing.T) {
				set(&u.Verifiers[1])

	if got, err := NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate(signedClaimsTestUpdate()); err != nil || got.Verifiers[0].HostIndexerID != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a pool-only update normalized to %+v, %v", got.Verifiers, err)
	}
}

		"node id of an snode": {func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) { member(u).NodeID = "snode-1" }, "verifiers: snode-1: node_id is an si_indexers snode_node_id"},

		"a host without a domain": {func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) {

// TestNormalizeSortsFailureDomainsAndChecksThemAgainstSIIndexers: the
// normalizer sorts the failure domains into a copy (nil when empty), wraps
// every Stage3Params.Validate refusal, needs tracks_enabled in the same
// update, refuses a domain of an indexer the update does not enrol and, once
// placement is on, an enrolled indexer without a domain.
func TestNormalizeSortsFailureDomainsAndChecksThemAgainstSIIndexers(t *testing.T) {
	u := stage3TestUpdate()
	callerDomains := slices.Clone(u.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains)
	got, err := NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate(u)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if want := []arbiter.IndexerFailureDomain{{IndexerID: 0, FailureDomain: "node:a"}, {IndexerID: 1, FailureDomain: "node:b"}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains, want) {
		t.Fatalf("domains = %+v, want %+v", got.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains, want)
	}
	if got.Stage3 == u.Stage3 || !reflect.DeepEqual(u.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains, callerDomains) {
		t.Fatal("normalization aliased or reordered the caller's stage3")
	}
	got.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains[0].FailureDomain = "mutated"
	if u.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains[1].FailureDomain != "node:a" {
		t.Fatal("the normalized domains alias the caller's slice")
	}
	empty := stage3TestUpdate()
	empty.Verifiers = empty.Verifiers[:3]
	empty.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains = []arbiter.IndexerFailureDomain{}
	if got, err := NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate(empty); err != nil || got.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains != nil {
		t.Fatalf("an empty domain list normalized to %#v, %v; want nil", got.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains, err)
	}
	placementOn := func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) {
		u.Stage3.Purge, u.Stage3.EvictionVoiding, u.Stage3.OwnerAwareSelection, u.Stage3.Placement = true, true, true, true
	}
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
		mutate func(*arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate)
		want   string
	}{
		"invalid parameter":  {func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) { u.Stage3.GroupSize = 0 }, "consensus params update: stage3: group_size must be at least 1"},
		"duplicate domain":   {func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) { u.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains[0].IndexerID = 0 }, "consensus params update: stage3: indexer_failure_domains must be sorted by indexer_id without duplicates"},
		"no tracks":          {func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) { u.TracksEnabled = false }, "consensus params update: stage3 requires tracks_enabled in the same update"},
		"unenrolled indexer": {func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) { u.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains[0].IndexerID = 5 }, "consensus params update: stage3: indexer_failure_domains names indexer 5, which has no si_indexers entry"},
		"placement without a domain": {func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) {
			placementOn(u)
			u.Verifiers = u.Verifiers[:3]
			u.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains = u.Stage3.IndexerFailureDomains[1:]
		}, "consensus params update: stage3: the placement switch needs a failure domain for every si_indexers entry; indexer 1 has none"},
	} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			u := stage3TestUpdate()
			tc.mutate(&u)
			if _, err := NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate(u); err == nil || err.Error() != tc.want {
				t.Fatalf("err = %v, want %q", err, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
	withPlacement := stage3TestUpdate()
	placementOn(&withPlacement)
	if _, err := NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate(withPlacement); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("placement with a domain for every indexer: %v", err)
	}
	without := stage3TestUpdate()
	without.Verifiers, without.Stage3 = without.Verifiers[:3], nil
	a, errA := ConsensusParamsUpdateHash(without)
	b, errB := ConsensusParamsUpdateHash(empty)
	if errA != nil || errB != nil || a == b {
		t.Fatalf("stage3 is not bound by the update hash: %s, %s (%v, %v)", a, b, errA, errB)
	}
}
```

```go
// normalizeStage3 returns a validated copy of the stage-3 parameter whose
// failure domains are sorted by indexer id (nil when empty) and name only
// indexers of the update's normalized si_indexers; once the placement switch
// is on they name every one. Absent stays nil. The activation, carry and
// one-way rules compare two parameters and are the FSM's.
func normalizeStage3(in *arbiter.Stage3Params, tracksEnabled bool, siIndexers []arbiter.SIIndexerEntry) (*arbiter.Stage3Params, error) {
	if in == nil {
		return nil, nil
	}
	p := *in
	p.IndexerFailureDomains = nilIfEmpty(slices.Clone(p.IndexerFailureDomains))
	slices.SortStableFunc(p.IndexerFailureDomains, func(a, b arbiter.IndexerFailureDomain) int { return cmp.Compare(a.IndexerID, b.IndexerID) })
	if err := p.Validate(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !tracksEnabled {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("stage3 requires tracks_enabled in the same update")
	}
	enrolled := make(map[uint64]bool, len(siIndexers))
	for _, e := range siIndexers {
		enrolled[e.IndexerID] = true
	}
	for _, d := range p.IndexerFailureDomains {
		if !enrolled[d.IndexerID] {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("stage3: indexer_failure_domains names indexer %d, which has no si_indexers entry", d.IndexerID)
		}
	}
	if p.Placement {
		for _, e := range siIndexers {
			if _, ok := p.FailureDomain(e.IndexerID); !ok {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("stage3: the placement switch needs a failure domain for every si_indexers entry; indexer %d has none", e.IndexerID)
			}
		}
	}
	return &p, nil
}
```

with:

```go
// normalizeVerifiers returns a validated deep copy sorted by node id that
// keeps every field (cloneVerifierEntry). An absent or empty list stays nil.
// A pool entry carries no stage-3 field, so it keeps the canonical form of
// every earlier digest; a member entry states every field (plan S3-E1 K58)
// and is checked against the update's normalized si_indexers and stage3.
// Consent, node-id use by registered nodes and the per-group floor are the
// FSM's.
func normalizeVerifiers(in []arbiter.VerifierEntry, siIndexers []arbiter.SIIndexerEntry, stage3 *arbiter.Stage3Params) ([]arbiter.VerifierEntry, error) {
	if len(in) == 0 {
		return nil, nil
	}
	out := make([]arbiter.VerifierEntry, len(in))
	for i, v := range in {
		if err := v.Validate(); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		e := cloneVerifierEntry(v)
		if err := validateVerifierStage3Fields(e); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		out[i] = e
	}
	slices.SortFunc(out, func(a, b arbiter.VerifierEntry) int { return strings.Compare(a.NodeID, b.NodeID) })
	keys := make(map[string]bool, len(out))
	signers := make(map[string]bool, len(out))
	for i, v := range out {
		if i > 0 && out[i-1].NodeID == v.NodeID {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("verifiers: duplicate node_id %q", v.NodeID)
		}
		if keys[string(v.Ed25519Pubkey)] {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s reuses another verifier's ed25519_pubkey", v.NodeID)
		}
		keys[string(v.Ed25519Pubkey)] = true
		if v.IsMember() {
			if signers[v.ReplicaSigner] {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s reuses another entry's replica_signer", v.NodeID)
			}
			signers[v.ReplicaSigner] = true
		}
	}
	hosts := make(map[uint64]bool, len(siIndexers))
	snodes := make(map[string]bool, len(siIndexers))
	for _, e := range siIndexers {
		hosts[e.IndexerID], snodes[e.SNodeNodeID] = true, true
	}
	for _, v := range out {
		if !v.IsMember() {
			continue
		}
		host := *v.HostIndexerID
		switch {
		case !hosts[host]:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: host_indexer_id %d has no si_indexers entry in this update", v.NodeID, host)
		case snodes[v.NodeID]:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: node_id is an si_indexers snode_node_id", v.NodeID)
		case stage3 == nil:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: an entry with host_indexer_id needs the stage3 parameter in the same update", v.NodeID)
		}
		if domain, _ := stage3.FailureDomain(host); domain != v.FailureDomain {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: failure_domain %q differs from stage3.indexer_failure_domains[%d] = %q", v.NodeID, v.FailureDomain, host, domain)
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

// cloneVerifierEntry copies every field of v, the key bytes and the host
// pointer detached from the caller's, with the replica signer lowercased.
func cloneVerifierEntry(v arbiter.VerifierEntry) arbiter.VerifierEntry {
	v.Ed25519Pubkey = bytes.Clone(v.Ed25519Pubkey)
	if v.HostIndexerID != nil {
		host := *v.HostIndexerID
		v.HostIndexerID = &host
	}
	v.ReplicaSigner = strings.ToLower(v.ReplicaSigner)
	return v
}

// validateVerifierStage3Fields checks the stage-3 fields one copied entry
// carries by itself (spec §6.1; plan S3-E1 K58).
func validateVerifierStage3Fields(e arbiter.VerifierEntry) error {
	if !e.IsMember() {
		if e.ReplicaSigner != "" || e.ConsentJWS != "" || e.Weight != 0 || e.FailureDomain != "" || e.Verify || e.Replicate || e.Counts || e.SharedRMT {
			return fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: an entry without host_indexer_id carries no replica_signer, consent_jws, weight, failure_domain or member flags", e.NodeID)
		}
		return nil
	}
	if _, err := normalizeSignerAddress(e.ReplicaSigner); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: replica_signer must be a non-zero lowercase 0x-prefixed 20-byte address", e.NodeID)
	}
	switch {
	case strings.TrimSpace(e.ConsentJWS) == "":
		return fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: consent_jws is required on an entry with host_indexer_id", e.NodeID)
	case e.Weight < 1 || e.Weight > 64:
		return fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: weight must be 1 to 64, got %d", e.NodeID, e.Weight)
	case !validFailureDomain(e.FailureDomain):
		return fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: failure_domain must be non-empty and free of whitespace and control characters", e.NodeID)
	case !e.Verify && !e.Replicate:
		return fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: a member entry needs verify or replicate", e.NodeID)
	case e.Counts && !e.Replicate:
		return fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: counts requires replicate", e.NodeID)
	case e.Verify && !e.SharedRMT:
		return fmt.Errorf("verifiers: %s: shared_rmt=false with verify=true is refused until the per-operator transport exists", e.NodeID)
	}
	return nil
}

// validFailureDomain is the rule of stage3.indexer_failure_domains and of a
// member's failure_domain: non-empty, no whitespace, no control character.
func validFailureDomain(d string) bool {
	return d != "" && !strings.ContainsFunc(d, func(r rune) bool { return unicode.IsSpace(r) || unicode.IsControl(r) })
}
```
