```go
package tableset

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/ddl"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// syncBuffer is a log sink the reconciler may write from any goroutine.
type syncBuffer struct {
	mu  sync.Mutex
	buf bytes.Buffer
}

func (b *syncBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.buf.Write(p)
}

func (b *syncBuffer) String() string {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.buf.String()
}

// auditedOwner is the owner SNode's reconciler (SweepDecommissioned) with a
// pinned clock and its log captured.
func auditedOwner(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, p ddl.Pinned, view *fakeView, arb *fakeArbiter) (*Reconciler, *testClock, *syncBuffer) {
	t.Helper()
	logs := &syncBuffer{}
	r := newReconciler(t, conn, p, view, arb, func(c *Config, d *Deps) {
		c.SweepDecommissioned = true
		d.Logger = slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(logs, nil))
	})
	return r, pinClock(r), logs
}

// strayRoot creates a replicated table at path on conn, in a database of the
// test's own.
func strayRoot(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, database, table, path string) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	if err := conn.Exec(ctx, "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS "+database); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = conn.Exec(context.Background(), "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "+database+" SYNC") })
	if err := conn.Exec(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("CREATE TABLE %s.%s (x UInt64) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('%s', 'stray') ORDER BY x", database, table, path)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func TestOwnerKeeperAuditReportsAnUnknownReplica(t *testing.T) {
	conn := requireCH(t)
	replicaConn := requireReplicaCH(t)
	p := isolatedPinned(t, conn, replicaConn)
	legacy, scoped := schemaFor(t, "legacy"), schemaFor(t, "scoped")
	scopedScope := ddl.KeeperScope{IncarnationSeq: 2, Scoped: true}
	owner := uint64(0)
	legacyInc := chainInc(t, 1, legacy, wire.TableStatusActive)
	scopedIncarnation := scopedInc(t, 2, scoped, wire.TableStatusActive)
	legacyInc.OwnerIndexerID, scopedIncarnation.OwnerIndexerID = &owner, &owner
	scopedIncarnation.PurgeMembers = []string{"member-c"}
	view, arb := newFakeView(), &fakeArbiter{nodeSet: []string{p.NodeID, "verifier-1"}}
	view.setSnap(wire.TableRegistrySnapshot{
		SIIndexers:   []arbiter.SIIndexerEntry{{IndexerID: 0, SNodeNodeID: p.NodeID}},
		Incarnations: []wire.TableIncarnation{legacyInc, scopedIncarnation},
		Groups: []wire.DatabaseGroup{{OwnerIndexerID: 0, DatabaseID: "db",
			Members: []wire.GroupMember{{NodeID: "member-b"}}, PastMembers: []string{"member-old"}}},
	})
	source, clock, logs := auditedOwner(t, conn, p, view, arb)
	mustReconcile(t, source)
	if st := source.Stats(); st.KeeperAuditRuns != 1 || len(st.KeeperFindings) != 0 || !source.Ready(legacy.TableID) || !source.Ready(scoped.TableID) {
		t.Fatalf("the first pass audits only the owner's own replicas: %+v", st)
	}
	// A pool verifier, a group member, a past member, the scoped
	// incarnation's purge member and an intruder each hold a replica of both
	// tables on the second server.
	for _, name := range []string{"verifier-1", "member-b", "member-old", "member-c", "intruder"} {
		q := peer(t, replicaConn, p, name)
		replicaOf(t, replicaConn, q, legacy, ddl.KeeperScope{IncarnationSeq: 1}, false)
		replicaOf(t, replicaConn, q, scoped, scopedScope, false)
	}
	mustReconcile(t, source)
	if runs := source.Stats().KeeperAuditRuns; runs != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("audit runs = %d before the interval passed, want 1", runs)
	}
	clock.advance(DefaultKeeperAuditInterval)
	mustReconcile(t, source)
	legacyPath := ddl.ZooKeeperPathFor(p.KeeperShardID, legacy.TableID, ddl.KeeperScope{})
	scopedPath := ddl.ZooKeeperPathFor(p.KeeperShardID, scoped.TableID, scopedScope)
	want := []KeeperFinding{
		{Path: legacyPath, Replica: "intruder", Reason: KeeperFindingUnknownReplica},
		{Path: legacyPath, Replica: "member-c", Reason: KeeperFindingUnknownReplica},
		{Path: scopedPath, Replica: "intruder", Reason: KeeperFindingUnknownReplica},
	}
	st := source.Stats()
	if st.KeeperAuditRuns != 2 || !reflect.DeepEqual(st.KeeperFindings, want) {
		t.Fatalf("audit runs %d, findings %+v; want 2 and %+v", st.KeeperAuditRuns, st.KeeperFindings, want)
	}
	line := "keeper replica on an owner path is not the owner, a pool verifier or a current or past member"
	if n := strings.Count(logs.String(), line); n != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("logged %d unknown-replica warnings, want 3:\n%s", n, logs.String())
	}
	if !strings.Contains(logs.String(), "table="+scoped.TableID+" path="+scopedPath+" replica=intruder") {
		t.Fatalf("the warning names the table, path and replica:\n%s", logs.String())
	}
	clock.advance(DefaultKeeperAuditInterval)
	mustReconcile(t, source)
	if st := source.Stats(); st.KeeperAuditRuns != 3 || !reflect.DeepEqual(st.KeeperFindings, want) || strings.Count(logs.String(), line) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("a repeated finding is kept and not logged again: %+v\n%s", st, logs.String())
	}
	nonOwner := newReconciler(t, conn, p, view, arb, nil)
	mustReconcile(t, nonOwner)
	if st := nonOwner.Stats(); st.KeeperAuditRuns != 0 || st.KeeperFindings != nil {
		t.Fatalf("only the owner (SweepDecommissioned) audits: %+v", st)
	}
}

func TestOwnerKeeperAuditReportsANonIncarnationRoot(t *testing.T) {
	conn := requireCH(t)
	p := isolatedPinned(t, conn)
	scoped, legacy := schemaFor(t, "scoped"), schemaFor(t, "legacy")
	view, arb := newFakeView(), &fakeArbiter{nodeSet: []string{p.NodeID}}
	view.set(scopedInc(t, 1, scoped, wire.TableStatusActive), chainInc(t, 2, legacy, wire.TableStatusActive))
	root := fmt.Sprintf("/sentio/%d/unsafe_inc", p.KeeperShardID)
	stray := "hg_stray_" + suffix(t)
	direct := "db__direct_" + suffix(t)
	strayRoot(t, conn, stray, "unknown_seq", root+"/"+ddl.CHTableName(scoped.TableID)+"/9")
	strayRoot(t, conn, stray, "unscoped_seq", root+"/"+ddl.CHTableName(legacy.TableID)+"/2")
	strayRoot(t, conn, stray, "bogus", root+"/"+ddl.CHTableName(scoped.TableID)+"/bogus")
	strayRoot(t, conn, stray, "direct", root+"/"+direct)
	source, _, logs := auditedOwner(t, conn, p, view, arb)
	mustReconcile(t, source)
	if !source.Ready(scoped.TableID) || !source.Ready(legacy.TableID) {
		t.Fatalf("not ready: %+v", source.Stats())
	}
	st := source.Stats()
	var paths []string
	for _, f := range st.KeeperFindings {
		if f.Reason != KeeperFindingNonIncarnationRoot || f.Replica != "" {
			t.Fatalf("finding %+v; every finding here is a non-incarnation root", f)
		}
		paths = append(paths, f.Path)
	}
	for _, want := range []string{
		root + "/" + ddl.CHTableName(scoped.TableID) + "/9",     // a canonical seq that is no incarnation
		root + "/" + ddl.CHTableName(scoped.TableID) + "/bogus", // not a seq
		root + "/" + ddl.CHTableName(legacy.TableID) + "/2",     // the seq of an incarnation that is not scoped
		root + "/" + direct, // a table created directly under unsafe_inc
		root + "/" + direct + "/replicas",
	} {
		if !slices.Contains(paths, want) {
			t.Fatalf("findings %v lack %s", paths, want)
		}
	}
	for _, path := range paths {
		if strings.HasPrefix(path, ddl.ZooKeeperPathFor(p.KeeperShardID, scoped.TableID, KeeperScopeOf(scopedInc(t, 1, scoped, wire.TableStatusActive)))) {
			t.Fatalf("the live incarnation's own path %s is reported", path)
		}
	}
	if !slices.IsSorted(paths) {
		t.Fatalf("findings are not sorted by path: %v", paths)
	}
	if n := strings.Count(logs.String(), "replicated-table root under the SI keeper roots is not an incarnation path"); n != len(paths) {
		t.Fatalf("logged %d non-incarnation-root warnings, want %d:\n%s", n, len(paths), logs.String())
	}
}

func TestOwnerKeeperAuditDropsNothing(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	conn := requireCH(t)
	replicaConn := requireReplicaCH(t)
	p := isolatedPinned(t, conn, replicaConn)
	scoped, legacy := schemaFor(t, "scoped"), schemaFor(t, "legacy")
	scopedScope := ddl.KeeperScope{IncarnationSeq: 1, Scoped: true}
	view, arb := newFakeView(), &fakeArbiter{nodeSet: []string{p.NodeID}}
	view.set(scopedInc(t, 1, scoped, wire.TableStatusActive), chainInc(t, 2, legacy, wire.TableStatusActive))
	source, clock, _ := auditedOwner(t, conn, p, view, arb)
	mustReconcile(t, source)
	// An attached and a detached intruder on both live paths, and a stray
	// root under unsafe_inc.
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		detach bool
	}{{"intruder-live", false}, {"intruder-gone", true}} {
		q := peer(t, replicaConn, p, tc.name)
		replicaOf(t, replicaConn, q, scoped, scopedScope, tc.detach)
		replicaOf(t, replicaConn, q, legacy, ddl.KeeperScope{IncarnationSeq: 2}, tc.detach)
	}
	strayRoot(t, conn, "hg_stray_"+suffix(t), "bogus", fmt.Sprintf("/sentio/%d/unsafe_inc/%s/bogus", p.KeeperShardID, ddl.CHTableName(scoped.TableID)))
	before := keeperRoots(t, conn, p)
	scopedBefore := replicasAt(t, conn, p, scoped.TableID, scopedScope)
	legacyBefore := replicasAt(t, conn, p, legacy.TableID, ddl.KeeperScope{})
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		clock.advance(DefaultKeeperAuditInterval)
		mustReconcile(t, source)
	}
	st := source.Stats()
	if st.KeeperAuditRuns != 4 || len(st.KeeperFindings) != 5 || st.LeftoverDrops != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v; want 4 audits, 5 findings (two intruders on two paths and the stray root), no drop", st)
	}
	if after := keeperRoots(t, conn, p); !reflect.DeepEqual(after, before) {
		t.Fatalf("roots changed under the audit:\n%+v\nwas\n%+v", after, before)
	}
	if got := replicasAt(t, conn, p, scoped.TableID, scopedScope); !slices.Equal(got, scopedBefore) || len(got) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("incarnation-path replicas = %v, were %v", got, scopedBefore)
	}
	if got := replicasAt(t, conn, p, legacy.TableID, ddl.KeeperScope{}); !slices.Equal(got, legacyBefore) || len(got) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("legacy replicas = %v, were %v", got, legacyBefore)
	}
	var active uint64
	if err := replicaConn.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count() FROM system.replicas WHERE replica_name = 'intruder-live' AND is_readonly = 0`).Scan(&active); err != nil || active != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("intruder-live's writable replicas = %d, %v; want both", active, err)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 25: Add the Keeper audit**

Create `dataplane/tableset/keeper_audit.go`:

```go
package tableset

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"sort"
	"time"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/ddl"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// DefaultKeeperAuditInterval paces the Keeper audit when
// Config.KeeperAuditInterval is 0.
const DefaultKeeperAuditInterval = 10 * time.Minute

// KeeperFindingReason is why the Keeper audit reports a path.
type KeeperFindingReason string

const (
	// KeeperFindingUnknownReplica: a replica on one of the owner's Keeper
	// paths that is not the owner, a node of the purge node set, a current
	// or past member of the incarnation's group, or one of its purge members
	// (wire.TableRegistrySnapshot.KnownKeeperReplica).
	KeeperFindingUnknownReplica KeeperFindingReason = "unknown_replica"
	// KeeperFindingNonIncarnationRoot: a replicated-table root under the
	// incarnation-scoped root that is not the path of a scoped_keeper_path
	// incarnation of its table (ddl.KeeperRoots.NonIncarnation, or a
	// canonical seq that names no such incarnation).
	KeeperFindingNonIncarnationRoot KeeperFindingReason = "non_incarnation_root"
)

// KeeperFinding is one report of the Keeper audit.
type KeeperFinding struct {
	Path    string
	Replica string // empty for a non-incarnation root
	Reason  KeeperFindingReason
}

// keeperFindingOf is a finding with the table key its log line names.
type keeperFindingOf struct {
	KeeperFinding
	table string
}

// auditKeeperIfDue runs the owner SNode's Keeper audit (housegate spec
// 2026-10-14 §8.2: the owner's sweep alerts on any replica on its paths that
// is not the owner, a pool verifier or a current or past member, and on any
// replicated-table root under the SI roots that is not an incarnation path)
// when Config.KeeperAuditInterval has passed since the last one that
// completed. It is report-only: it drops nothing, whatever it finds; the
// sweeps keep their own rules. Each finding is logged when it first appears;
// Stats carries the last audit's findings. A failed audit is logged and
// retried at the next pass.
func (r *Reconciler) auditKeeperIfDue(ctx context.Context, snap wire.TableRegistrySnapshot) {
	if !r.cfg.SweepDecommissioned {
		return
	}
	now := r.now()
	r.mu.Lock()
	due := r.lastKeeperAudit.IsZero() || !now.Before(r.lastKeeperAudit.Add(r.cfg.KeeperAuditInterval))
	r.mu.Unlock()
	if !due {
		return
	}
	found, err := r.auditKeeper(ctx, snap)
	if err != nil {
		r.d.Logger.Warn("keeper audit failed; the next pass retries it", "err", err)
		return
	}
	var findings []KeeperFinding
	for _, f := range found {
		findings = append(findings, f.KeeperFinding)
	}
	r.mu.Lock()
	previous := r.keeperFindings
	r.keeperFindings = findings
	r.keeperAuditRuns++
	r.lastKeeperAudit = now
	r.mu.Unlock()
	for _, f := range found {
		if slices.Contains(previous, f.KeeperFinding) {
			continue
		}
		switch f.Reason {
		case KeeperFindingUnknownReplica:
			r.d.Logger.Warn("keeper replica on an owner path is not the owner, a pool verifier or a current or past member",
				"table", f.table, "path", f.Path, "replica", f.Replica)
		case KeeperFindingNonIncarnationRoot:
			r.d.Logger.Warn("replicated-table root under the SI keeper roots is not an incarnation path", "path", f.Path)
		}
	}
}

// auditKeeper lists both SI Keeper roots of this node's shard and returns the
// findings, sorted by path then replica. This node's paths are the legacy
// path of every incarnation it owns that is not scoped (a legacy path is
// judged against every such incarnation of its physical name) and the
// incarnation path of every scoped incarnation it owns; another owner's
// paths are that owner's to audit. Every root under unsafe_inc that is no
// incarnation path is reported whoever owns its name.
func (r *Reconciler) auditKeeper(ctx context.Context, snap wire.TableRegistrySnapshot) ([]keeperFindingOf, error) {
	shard := r.cfg.Pinned.KeeperShardID
	roots, err := ddl.ListKeeperRoots(ctx, r.d.Conn, shard)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	legacyIncs := map[string][]wire.TableIncarnation{}
	for _, inc := range snap.Incarnations {
		if inc.ScopedKeeperPath || !r.owns(snap, inc) {
			continue
		}
		physical := ddl.CHTableName(inc.Key())
		legacyIncs[physical] = append(legacyIncs[physical], inc)
	}
	var nodes []string
	fetched := false
	var out []keeperFindingOf
	check := func(key string, s ddl.KeeperScope, incs []wire.TableIncarnation) error {
		replicas, err := ddl.KeeperReplicasAt(ctx, r.d.Conn, shard, key, s)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		for _, replica := range replicas {
			if replica == r.cfg.Pinned.NodeID {
				continue
			}
			if !fetched {
				if nodes, err = r.d.Arbiter.PurgeNodeSet(ctx); err != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("tableset: purge node set: %w", err)
				}
				fetched = true
			}
			if slices.ContainsFunc(incs, func(inc wire.TableIncarnation) bool { return snap.KnownKeeperReplica(inc, nodes, replica) }) {
				continue
			}
			out = append(out, keeperFindingOf{
				KeeperFinding: KeeperFinding{Path: ddl.ZooKeeperPathFor(shard, key, s), Replica: replica, Reason: KeeperFindingUnknownReplica},
				table:         key,
			})
		}
		return nil
	}
	for _, physical := range roots.Legacy {
		incs := legacyIncs[physical]
		if len(incs) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		if err := check(incs[len(incs)-1].Key(), ddl.KeeperScope{}, incs); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	for _, path := range roots.Scoped {
		inc := incarnation(snap, path.IncarnationSeq)
		if inc == nil || !inc.ScopedKeeperPath || ddl.CHTableName(inc.Key()) != path.Table {
			out = append(out, keeperFindingOf{KeeperFinding: KeeperFinding{
				Path:   fmt.Sprintf("/sentio/%d/%s/%s/%d", shard, ddl.KeeperScopedUnsafeRoot, path.Table, path.IncarnationSeq),
				Reason: KeeperFindingNonIncarnationRoot,
			}})
			continue
		}
		if !r.owns(snap, *inc) {
			continue
		}
		if err := check(inc.Key(), KeeperScopeOf(*inc), []wire.TableIncarnation{*inc}); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	for _, path := range roots.NonIncarnation {
		out = append(out, keeperFindingOf{KeeperFinding: KeeperFinding{Path: path, Reason: KeeperFindingNonIncarnationRoot}})
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
		if out[i].Path != out[j].Path {
			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
		}
		return out[i].Replica < out[j].Replica
	})
	return out, nil
}
```

## Task 62: arbiter-core — `dataplane/evidence`, the member verify role, the quiescence ledger and the `hg_member_unsafe` reconciler (S3-E1)

Spec §8.1 (the si-member contains the verifier role: replay, byte scan, evidence), §8.2 (`si_member_ddl` creates and drops the member's replicas and nothing else; `si_member` does everything else; neither holds `SYSTEM DROP REPLICA`; a leaked `si_member_ddl` can drop a table above a later incarnation's path), §8.3 (the member intent set, "checked like `hg_unsafe`", the group-scoped reconciler that creates replicas as `si_member_ddl` only while the node is registered, not evicted and the purge rule is on), §8.5 last paragraph (replay scratch in `hg_rstage` under the member's prefix), §8.8 (a member drops its `hg_member_unsafe` replica only at Purging, after its quiescence hook confirms that no unresolved block of its verify sets references the table), §10.4 steps 4 and 6, §15 (the arbiter-core line), §17 (the member users' confinement); contract §42.2 and the Task 62 part of §42.3; clarification K66; decisions D30 and D36. This task, in arbiter-core on the branch of Tasks 59–61:

- extracts the network verifier's evidence path into the new package `dataplane/evidence` — the replay and byte-side scan handler with its submissions and log lines, the ClickHouse scanner over a named database, the replay core over a given materializer, the durable `registration_seq` and the signed VERIFIER registration — and makes `verifier` delegate to it byte for byte (the same submitted bytes, log texts and fields, `registration.json` name and shape), pinned against bytes captured from the verifier at arbiter-core `v0.15.0`;
- adds the package `member/consensus`: `Config` and `ReconcilerConfig` with the defaults and file names of contract §42.3; the verify role, which registers the member as a VERIFIER only with `Config.Register` (S3-F step 4) and answers its dispatch through an `evidence.Handler` that scans `hg_member_unsafe`, replays into `hg_rstage` under `install.ScratchPrefix(NodeID, bootNonce) + "v"`, refuses a job whose tables have no verified local replica at their incarnation's Keeper path, and writes the quiescence ledger before every replay; the quiescence ledger itself (`quiescence.json`, durable, resolved through `GetBlockVerification`); and the `hg_member_unsafe` reconciler that runs as `si_member_ddl`, creates a replica only with `CreateReplicas` (S3-F step 6), registration, the purge switch and placement, keeps it through Retiring, drops it at Purging or after a released Leaving record only once its table is quiet, stops on `REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS` and never runs `SYSTEM DROP REPLICA`;
- replaces Plan S3-C2's guard `TestMemberUnsafeIntentHasNoCallerInP2` (Task 30 says Task 62 does, when it adds the first caller) with a guard that `ddl.MemberUnsafeIntent` is named only by this reconciler and the verify role's readiness check;
- proves on the fenced 26.3 server of Plan S3-C2's confinement harness (with `table_engines_require_grant`, the embedded Keeper and the `si_member_ddl` profile) that the replay scratch lives in `hg_rstage` under the member prefix with no refusal as `si_member`, that the reconciler's replica as `si_member_ddl` fetches the owner's parts byte for byte at the incarnation path and is dropped at Purging leaving the owner's table and Keeper replica intact, and that a stale replica named after the member stops the reconciler and is left in place; the runner `scripts/ci/clickhouse-member-confinement.sh` now also requires these `TestMember*` tests.

Nothing here is wired into `member.Role` or runs on a host: Task 63 sets `member.Config.Consensus` and wires the verify role, and Plan S3-E4 Task 79 runs the reconciler process (decision D30). Task 63 pushes the branch and opens the one PR of Tasks 59–63.

Notes:
- **Base and anchors.** The worktree is Task 59's, `$HOME/src/remotesrc/claude/arbiter-core/multi-source-s3e1` on `urwt/claude/multi-source-s3e1`, after Task 61's last commit; under it is `CORE_TAG_P4` (Plan S3-D Task 50). Line anchors are those of arbiter-core `origin/main` `cfd4f42` (`v0.15.0`, Plan S3-A); its `verifier/*.go` sources equal the header's `8f0bc43`, and no plan between them and this task changes a `verifier` source file (Plans S3-C1, S3-C2 and S3-C4 add packages and leave `verifier/backends.go:21-41` as the model of their own replay cores), so every `verifier` hunk below applies as written. `dataplane/ddl/member_test.go` and `dataplane/ddl/BUILD.bazel` are Plan S3-C2 Task 30's text, and `member/confinement/` and `scripts/ci/clickhouse-member-confinement.sh` Plan S3-C2 Task 34's; their anchors are that text (hunk rule).
- **Byte for byte (contract §42.2).** `evidence.Handler` is `verifier/verifier.go:327-347` and `:413-448` moved verbatim: the same `ReplayJobFromPB`, the add gate before the replay, the same `SubmitAttestation` and `SubmitByteSideScan` requests, the same `CanonicalDigest(arbiter.DomainByteSideScan, …)` scan hash and ed25519 signature, and the same four warn lines with the same fields; `evidence.NewReplayCore` is `backends.go:20-42` with the materializer passed in (the verifier passes `chexec.NewMaterializer`, unchanged: arbiter's `cmd/arbiter-verifier` relies on its unqualified scratch); `evidence.CHScanner` is `backends.go:71-162` with the database a field; `evidence.RegistrationSeq` is `registration_state.go:10-92` with its error texts and temp-file name; `VerifierRegistrationRequests` is `claims.go:37-56`. `TestEvidenceHandlerSubmitsWhatTheVerifierSubmitted` and `TestVerifierRoleDelegatesToTheEvidenceHandler` pin the two submissions to bytes captured from the unmodified verifier of `v0.15.0` (`proto.MarshalOptions{Deterministic: true}`, hex), and `TestVerifierRegistrationFileKeepsItsShape` pins `{"registration_seq":N}` and that a file the old verifier wrote stays the floor.
- **Why the verify role, not the reconciler, verifies the replica.** As `si_member_ddl` ClickHouse 26.3 shows `system.tables` (name, comment, `engine_full`) for `hg_member_unsafe`, answers `system.columns` with no rows, and refuses `system.replicas`, `system.zookeeper` and `system.detached_tables` with 497 (measured on 26.3.51.7 with `table_engines_require_grant` and `SI_MEMBER_DDL_GRANTS`, Appendix B), so `ddl.VerifyProtocolTable` cannot run as that user. The reconciler therefore attributes a table by its `hg_incarnation=` comment and the head of its `engine_full` (`ReplicatedMergeTree('<incarnation path>', '<node id>')`), and the verify role's gate runs the full `ddl.VerifyProtocolTable` against `ddl.MemberUnsafeIntent` at the incarnation's path as `si_member` (which holds `SELECT ON hg_member_unsafe.*` and `SELECT ON system.replicas`) before every attestation, so a scan never reads a missing, stale-incarnation, wrong-path or drifted replica. The gate covers every statement's table and every table a table-set transition adds, like the verifier's add gate, and never waits (the arbiter re-dispatches every `dispatch.retry_interval`).
- **The quiescence ledger (spec §8.8).** The handler runs `Observe` before the gate and the replay: the role writes (block, table, live incarnation) for every table the job names into `quiescence.json` (temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync) before anything reads the replica, so the reconciler process, which reads the file through the member state volume, never drops a replica a dispatched block may still scan. A block resolves once `GetBlockVerification` shows `verdict_evaluated` (the quorum latched) or the node is no longer in its `verifier_set` (re-selected away); `Run` resolves every `ResolveInterval`, also without `Register`, so a ledger an earlier registered run left still drains. A block the arbiter cannot serve stays in the ledger.
- **What the reconciler never drops.** A table it cannot attribute — no incarnation comment, an unknown incarnation, or an `engine_full` that is not this member's replica at that incarnation's exact path — is logged once and left for an operator: dropping the last replica of a table above a later incarnation's path would delete that incarnation's Keeper subtree (spec §8.2). It drops its own replicas only with `DROP TABLE … SYNC`, never `SYSTEM DROP REPLICA` (it holds no such right), and only once `ReadQuiescence(StateDir).Quiet(table, seq)`; an unreadable ledger keeps every replica. On `REPLICA_ALREADY_EXISTS` (253) it stops that incarnation for the life of the process with `ErrReplicaAlreadyExists` and the contract's text, counts it, logs it at error level, and goes on with the other tables; the owner's sweep removes such a replica after the member is evicted (spec §8.8).
- **The replay prefix.** `ReplayScratchPrefix(nodeID, bootNonce)` is `install.ScratchPrefix(nodeID, bootNonce) + "v"`: under `install.NodePrefix`, so S3-C2's startup drop removes every earlier boot's replay scratch, and distinct from the shadow's `…r` and from every `install.ScratchName` (`…<decimal>`). The materializer issues only `CREATE TABLE … ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple()`, a batch `INSERT`, a `SELECT` and `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` on it, all inside `si_member`'s `hg_rstage` rights (decision D36), which `TestMemberReplayScratchLivesInRstageUnderTheMemberPrefix` records statement by statement.
- **Beyond contract §42.2–§42.3** (recorded in Appendix B, Task 62): `evidence.Deps.NotReadyLog` (the warn text of a `TablesReady` refusal; empty is the verifier's `table-set transition adds a table this verifier has not created; refusing to attest`), `(*evidence.CHScanner).Database`, `Registry` and `SchemaFor` (the verifier's `checkScannerRegistry` and its existing tests reach the scanner through them now that `verifier.CHScanner` is an alias); `consensus.VerifyDeps.BootNonce` (`member.Role`'s boot nonce, which the contract's prefix needs and neither `Config` nor `VerifyDeps` carried); `consensus.ReconcilerConfig.NetworkID`, `Tables` and `StoragePolicy` (the reconciler resolves each incarnation's schema with `dataplane.IncarnationSchema` and creates its replica with the member storage policy; Plan S3-E4 Task 79 sets them from the member configuration it already reads); `consensus.ReplayScratchPrefix` and `consensus.NewReplayMaterializer` (the verify role's own materializer, which the confinement test drives as `si_member`); the unexported `errRegisterOff` text `member consensus: Register is off`; the tests named in **Interfaces**; the guard `TestMemberUnsafeIntentIsCalledOnlyByTheMemberConsensusMode` replacing Plan S3-C2's `TestMemberUnsafeIntentHasNoCallerInP2`; the pre-existing `verifier` tests `TestNewScanner_DefaultsUnsafeDatabaseAndMapsTableName` (`scanner.Database()` for `scanner.cfg.UnsafeDatabase`), the nine `.schemaFor(` calls of `registry_test.go` (now `.SchemaFor(`) and its helper `newGateRoleV` (`withEvidenceV`), each edited only where it reached a field that moved; and the runner's required list.

```go
package evidence

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"log/slog"
	"net"
	"slices"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"
	"github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2/lib/driver"
	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"
	"google.golang.org/grpc"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/proto"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane"
)

// gatewayFake is a VerifierGateway and Membership server that records every
// submission and registration, and rejects submissions with rejectErr when it
// is set.
type gatewayFake struct {
	pb.UnimplementedVerifierGatewayServer
	pb.UnimplementedMembershipServer

	mu           sync.Mutex
	attestations []*pb.ReplayAttestation
	scans        []*pb.ByteSideScanMsg
	regs         []*pb.NodeRegistration
	marks        []*pb.NodeRef
	rejectErr    error
}

func (f *gatewayFake) SubmitAttestation(_ context.Context, m *pb.ReplayAttestation) (*pb.Ack, error) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.attestations = append(f.attestations, m)
	if f.rejectErr != nil {
		return nil, f.rejectErr
	}
	return &pb.Ack{}, nil
}

func (f *gatewayFake) SubmitByteSideScan(_ context.Context, m *pb.ByteSideScanMsg) (*pb.Ack, error) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.scans = append(f.scans, m)
	if f.rejectErr != nil {
		return nil, f.rejectErr
	}
	return &pb.Ack{}, nil
}

func (f *gatewayFake) RegisterNode(_ context.Context, m *pb.NodeRegistration) (*pb.Ack, error) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.regs = append(f.regs, m)
	return &pb.Ack{}, nil
}

func (f *gatewayFake) MarkActive(_ context.Context, m *pb.NodeRef) (*pb.Ack, error) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.marks = append(f.marks, m)
	return &pb.Ack{}, nil
}

func (f *gatewayFake) submitted() ([]*pb.ReplayAttestation, []*pb.ByteSideScanMsg) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return slices.Clone(f.attestations), slices.Clone(f.scans)
}

// startGatewayFake serves f on a loopback port and returns a client for it.
func startGatewayFake(t *testing.T, f *gatewayFake) *dataplane.Client {
	t.Helper()
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	srv := grpc.NewServer()
	pb.RegisterVerifierGatewayServer(srv, f)
	pb.RegisterMembershipServer(srv, f)
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		_ = srv.Serve(ln)
		close(done)
	}()
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		srv.Stop()
		<-done
	})
	client, err := dataplane.New(dataplane.Config{Peers: []dataplane.Peer{{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: ln.Addr().String()}}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(client.Close)
	return client
}

// replayFake answers every job with att (or err) and records the jobs; before,
// when set, runs first inside Verify.
type replayFake struct {
	mu     sync.Mutex
	jobs   []replay.ReplayJob
	att    replay.ReplayAttestation
	err    error
	before func(job replay.ReplayJob)
}

func (r *replayFake) Verify(_ context.Context, job replay.ReplayJob) (replay.ReplayAttestation, error) {
	if r.before != nil {
		r.before(job)
	}
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	r.jobs = append(r.jobs, job)
	return r.att, r.err
}

func (r *replayFake) count() int {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	return len(r.jobs)
}

// scannerFake answers every scan with scans (or err) and records the parts.
type scannerFake struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	parts [][]arbiter.PartRef
	scans []arbiter.PartScan
	err   error
}

func (s *scannerFake) Scan(_ context.Context, parts []arbiter.PartRef) ([]arbiter.PartScan, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.parts = append(s.parts, slices.Clone(parts))
	return slices.Clone(s.scans), s.err
}

// queryRecorder is a clickhouse.Conn whose only method is Query: it records
// the statement and answers err. Any other method panics (nil embedded Conn).
type queryRecorder struct {
	clickhouse.Conn
	mu      sync.Mutex
	queries []string
	err     error
}

func (c *queryRecorder) Query(_ context.Context, query string, _ ...any) (driver.Rows, error) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	c.queries = append(c.queries, query)
	return nil, c.err
}

func (c *queryRecorder) recorded() []string {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	return slices.Clone(c.queries)
}

// syncBuffer is a goroutine-safe log sink.
type syncBuffer struct {
	mu  sync.Mutex
	buf bytes.Buffer
}

func (b *syncBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.buf.Write(p)
}

func (b *syncBuffer) String() string {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.buf.String()
}

func textLogger(w *syncBuffer) *slog.Logger { return slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(w, nil)) }

func marshalDeterministic(t *testing.T, m proto.Message) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	b, err := proto.MarshalOptions{Deterministic: true}.Marshal(m)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return b
}
```

```go
}

// newFrozenHandler is verifier-1's handler over fakes that answer the frozen
// inputs; deps edits its Deps before NewHandler.
func newFrozenHandler(t *testing.T, gw *gatewayFake, deps func(*Deps)) (*Handler, *replayFake, *scannerFake) {
	t.Helper()
	core := &replayFake{att: frozenAttestation}
	scanner := &scannerFake{scans: frozenScans}
	d := Deps{Client: startGatewayFake(t, gw), Replay: core, Scanner: scanner}
	if deps != nil {
		deps(&d)
	}
	h, err := NewHandler(Config{ReplicaID: authoritytest.VerifierNodeID(1), Ed25519Seed: authoritytest.VerifierKey(1).Seed()}, d)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return h, core, scanner
}

func TestEvidenceHandlerSubmitsWhatTheVerifierSubmitted(t *testing.T) {
	gw := &gatewayFake{}
	h, _, scanner := newFrozenHandler(t, gw, nil)
	if err := h.HandleReplayJob(context.Background(), wire.ReplayJobToPB(frozenJob)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := h.HandleScanRequest(context.Background(), frozenScanRequest()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	atts, scans := gw.submitted()
	if len(atts) != 1 || len(scans) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d attestations and %d scans submitted, want one each", len(atts), len(scans))
	}
	if got := hex.EncodeToString(marshalDeterministic(t, atts[0])); got != frozenAttestationHex {
		t.Fatalf("attestation = %s, want the verifier's %s", got, frozenAttestationHex)
	}
	if got := hex.EncodeToString(marshalDeterministic(t, scans[0])); got != frozenScanHex {
		t.Fatalf("scan = %s, want the verifier's %s", got, frozenScanHex)
	}
	if len(scanner.parts) != 1 || fmt.Sprint(scanner.parts[0]) != fmt.Sprint(frozenScanParts) {
		t.Fatalf("scanner asked for %v, want %v", scanner.parts, frozenScanParts)
	}
}

func TestEvidenceHandlerRunsObserveFirstAndRefusesWhenItFails(t *testing.T) {
	var order []string
	observeErr := errors.New("test: ledger write failed")
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name    string
		observe error
		want    []string
	}{
		{"observe succeeds", nil, []string{"observe", "ready", "replay"}},
		{"observe fails", observeErr, []string{"observe"}},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			order = nil
			logs := &syncBuffer{}
			gw := &gatewayFake{}
			h, core, _ := newFrozenHandler(t, gw, func(d *Deps) {
				d.Observe = func(job replay.ReplayJob) error {
					order = append(order, "observe")
					if job.BlockSeq != frozenJob.BlockSeq {
						t.Errorf("observed block %d, want %d", job.BlockSeq, frozenJob.BlockSeq)
					}
					return tc.observe
				}
				d.TablesReady = func(context.Context, replay.ReplayJob) error {
					order = append(order, "ready")
					return nil
				}
				d.NotReady = errNotReadyForTest
				d.Logger = textLogger(logs)
			})
			core.before = func(replay.ReplayJob) { order = append(order, "replay") }
			err := h.HandleReplayJob(context.Background(), wire.ReplayJobToPB(frozenJob))
			if !errors.Is(err, tc.observe) {
				t.Fatalf("HandleReplayJob = %v, want %v", err, tc.observe)
			}
			if strings.Join(order, ",") != strings.Join(tc.want, ",") {
				t.Fatalf("order = %v, want %v", order, tc.want)
			}
			atts, _ := gw.submitted()
			if tc.observe != nil {
				if len(atts) != 0 || core.count() != 0 {
					t.Fatalf("a failed observer still replayed (%d) or submitted (%d)", core.count(), len(atts))
				}
				if !strings.Contains(logs.String(), "evidence observer failed; refusing to attest") {
					t.Fatalf("logs = %s", logs.String())
				}
			} else if len(atts) != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("%d attestations, want 1", len(atts))
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestEvidenceHandlerGatesTheReplayOnTablesReady(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name    string
		ready   error
		log     string
		wantLog string
	}{
		{"not ready, the verifier's text", fmt.Errorf("%w: block 9 adds [db.n]", errNotReadyForTest), "",
			"table-set transition adds a table this verifier has not created; refusing to attest"},
		{"not ready, the caller's text", fmt.Errorf("%w: db.t", errNotReadyForTest), "member: no replica; refusing to attest",
			"member: no replica; refusing to attest"},
		{"the context ended", context.Canceled, "", ""},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			logs := &syncBuffer{}
			gw := &gatewayFake{}
			h, core, _ := newFrozenHandler(t, gw, func(d *Deps) {
				d.TablesReady = func(context.Context, replay.ReplayJob) error { return tc.ready }
				d.NotReady = errNotReadyForTest
				d.NotReadyLog = tc.log
				d.Logger = textLogger(logs)
			})
			if err := h.HandleReplayJob(context.Background(), wire.ReplayJobToPB(frozenJob)); !errors.Is(err, tc.ready) {
				t.Fatalf("HandleReplayJob = %v, want %v", err, tc.ready)
			}
			if atts, _ := gw.submitted(); core.count() != 0 || len(atts) != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("a refused job replayed (%d) or submitted (%d)", core.count(), len(atts))
			}
			switch {
			case tc.wantLog == "" && strings.Contains(logs.String(), "refusing to attest"):
				t.Fatalf("an ended context was logged as a refusal: %s", logs.String())
			case tc.wantLog != "" && !strings.Contains(logs.String(), `msg="`+tc.wantLog+`"`):
				t.Fatalf("logs = %s, want %q", logs.String(), tc.wantLog)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestEvidenceHandlerLogsWhatItRefusesAndWhatTheArbiterRejects(t *testing.T) {
	logs := &syncBuffer{}
	gw := &gatewayFake{rejectErr: status.Error(codes.InvalidArgument, "scan_hash does not match the scan body")}
	h, _, _ := newFrozenHandler(t, gw, func(d *Deps) { d.Logger = textLogger(logs) })
	if err := h.HandleScanRequest(context.Background(), frozenScanRequest()); status.Code(err) != codes.InvalidArgument {
		t.Fatalf("HandleScanRequest = %v, want the arbiter's InvalidArgument", err)
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`msg="arbiter did not accept verifier evidence"`, "kind=\"byte-side scan\"", "block=9", "replica=verifier-1", "code=InvalidArgument", "scan_hash=0x2713bfcb", "parts=2"} {
		if !strings.Contains(logs.String(), want) {
			t.Fatalf("logs = %s, want %s", logs.String(), want)
		}
	}

	logs = &syncBuffer{}
	h, _, _ = newFrozenHandler(t, &gatewayFake{}, func(d *Deps) {
		d.Replay = &replayFake{err: errors.New("test: replay failed")}
		d.Scanner = &scannerFake{err: errors.New("test: scan failed")}
		d.Logger = textLogger(logs)
	})
	if err := h.HandleReplayJob(context.Background(), wire.ReplayJobToPB(frozenJob)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("a failed replay was attested")
	}
	if err := h.HandleScanRequest(context.Background(), frozenScanRequest()); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("a failed scan was submitted")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`msg="replay verify failed; refusing to attest"`, `msg="byte-side scan failed; refusing to attest"`} {
		if !strings.Contains(logs.String(), want) {
			t.Fatalf("logs = %s, want %s", logs.String(), want)
		}
	}
}

func TestNewHandlerRefusesAnIncompleteConfig(t *testing.T) {
	client, err := dataplane.New(dataplane.Config{Peers: []dataplane.Peer{{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: "127.0.0.1:1"}}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer client.Close()
	seed := authoritytest.VerifierKey(1).Seed()
	full := Deps{Client: client, Replay: &replayFake{}, Scanner: &scannerFake{}}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name string
		cfg  Config
		deps Deps
		want string
	}{
		{"no replica id", Config{Ed25519Seed: seed}, full, "evidence: replica id is required"},
		{"a short seed", Config{ReplicaID: "v1", Ed25519Seed: seed[:31]}, full, "evidence: ed25519 seed must be 32 bytes"},
		{"no client", Config{ReplicaID: "v1", Ed25519Seed: seed}, Deps{Replay: full.Replay, Scanner: full.Scanner}, "evidence: client, replay core, and scanner are required"},
		{"no scanner", Config{ReplicaID: "v1", Ed25519Seed: seed}, Deps{Client: client, Replay: full.Replay}, "evidence: client, replay core, and scanner are required"},
		{"a gate without its sentinel", Config{ReplicaID: "v1", Ed25519Seed: seed},
			Deps{Client: client, Replay: full.Replay, Scanner: full.Scanner, TablesReady: func(context.Context, replay.ReplayJob) error { return nil }},
			"evidence: TablesReady needs the NotReady sentinel it wraps"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if _, err := NewHandler(tc.cfg, tc.deps); err == nil || err.Error() != tc.want {
				t.Fatalf("NewHandler = %v, want %q", err, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package evidence

// staticView is an enabled registry view of one snapshot.
type staticView struct{ snap wire.TableRegistrySnapshot }

func (v staticView) View() (wire.TableRegistrySnapshot, bool) { return v.snap, true }
func (v staticView) Changed() <-chan struct{}                 { return make(chan struct{}) }
func (v staticView) Ready() <-chan struct{} {
	ch := make(chan struct{})
	close(ch)
	return ch
}

func TestCHScannerScansItsDatabaseThroughTheRegistry(t *testing.T) {
	genesis := payloadexec.TableSchema{TableID: "db.g", Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "v", Type: "UInt64"}}}
	chain := payloadexec.TableSchema{TableID: "db.c", Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "w", Type: "String"}}}
	schemaJSON, err := json.Marshal(chain)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	view := staticView{snap: wire.TableRegistrySnapshot{Incarnations: []wire.TableIncarnation{
		{Seq: 1, DatabaseID: "db", TableID: "g", Origin: wire.TableOriginGenesis, Status: wire.TableStatusActive},
		{Seq: 2, DatabaseID: "db", TableID: "c", Origin: wire.TableOriginChain, Status: wire.TableStatusActive,
			SchemaJSON: string(schemaJSON), SchemaHash: payloadexec.TableSchemaHash("testnet", chain)},
	}}}
	conn := &queryRecorder{err: errors.New("test: no server")}
	s := NewCHScanner("testnet", []payloadexec.TableSchema{genesis}, "hg_member_unsafe", conn, view)
	if s.Database() != "hg_member_unsafe" || s.Registry() == nil {
		t.Fatalf("scanner reads %q with registry %v", s.Database(), s.Registry())
	}
	_, err = s.Scan(context.Background(), []arbiter.PartRef{{TableID: "db.c", PartitionID: "all", PartRowLtHash: "0xh", PartName: "all_1_1_0"}})
	if err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "scan table db.c: part scan query: test: no server") {
		t.Fatalf("Scan = %v", err)
	}
	queries := conn.recorded()
	if len(queries) != 1 || !strings.Contains(queries[0], "SELECT _part, _hg_row_id, `w` FROM `hg_member_unsafe`.`db__c` WHERE _part IN (") {
		t.Fatalf("queries = %q: want the chain schema's columns from hg_member_unsafe", queries)
	}
	if _, err := s.Scan(context.Background(), []arbiter.PartRef{{TableID: "db.c", PartitionID: "all"}}); err == nil ||
		err.Error() != "scan request part without a name (table db.c partition all)" {
		t.Fatalf("a part without a name gave %v", err)
	}
}
```

```go
package evidence

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"testing"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority/authoritytest"
)

func TestRegistrationSeqIsDurableAndNeverGoesBack(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	seq := NewRegistrationSeq(dir)
	readFile := func() string {
		t.Helper()
		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, RegistrationStateFile))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return string(b)
	}
	next := func(r *RegistrationSeq, now uint64) uint64 {
		t.Helper()
		n, err := r.Next(now)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return n
	}
	if got := next(seq, 1_000); got != 1_000 || readFile() != `{"registration_seq":1000}` {
		t.Fatalf("first seq %d, file %s: want the clock and its record", got, readFile())
	}
	if got := next(seq, 10); got != 1_001 {
		t.Fatalf("a clock that went back gave %d, want last+1", got)
	}
	// A new process on the same directory continues from the file.
	if got := next(NewRegistrationSeq(dir), 10); got != 1_002 || readFile() != `{"registration_seq":1002}` {
		t.Fatalf("a restarted sequence gave %d, file %s", got, readFile())
	}
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil || len(entries) != 1 || entries[0].Name() != RegistrationStateFile {
		t.Fatalf("state dir holds %v (%v), want only %s", entries, err, RegistrationStateFile)
	}
	// In memory: clock-floored, never back, nothing written.
	mem := NewRegistrationSeq("")
	if a, b := next(mem, 50), next(mem, 40); a != 50 || b != 51 {
		t.Fatalf("in-memory seqs %d, %d, want 50, 51", a, b)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, RegistrationStateFile), []byte("{"), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := NewRegistrationSeq(dir).Next(1); err == nil || err.Error() != "verifier registration state corrupt: unexpected end of JSON input" {
		t.Fatalf("a corrupt file gave %v", err)
	}
}

func TestVerifierRegistrationRequestsAreSignedWithTheEvidenceKey(t *testing.T) {
	reg, mark, err := VerifierRegistrationRequests(authoritytest.VerifierKey(1), authoritytest.VerifierNodeID(1),
		authoritytest.RegistrationSeq, authoritytest.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// ed25519 is deterministic: the requests reproduce the pinned vectors.
	if reg.GetNodeId() != authoritytest.VerifierNodeID(1) || !slices.Equal(reg.GetRoles(), []pb.NodeRole{pb.NodeRole_NODE_ROLE_VERIFIER}) ||
		reg.GetRegistrationSeq() != authoritytest.RegistrationSeq || reg.GetEd25519Signature() != authoritytest.VerifierRegistrationSignature ||
		mark.GetNodeId() != authoritytest.VerifierNodeID(1) || mark.GetRegistrationSeq() != authoritytest.RegistrationSeq ||
		mark.GetEd25519Signature() != authoritytest.VerifierMarkActiveSignature {
		t.Fatalf("registration %v / activation %v differ from the authoritytest vectors", reg, mark)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(reg.GetFeatures(), arbiter.LocalNodeFeatures()) || reg.GetSignerJws() != "" {
		t.Fatalf("registration %v must advertise %v and carry no signer JWS", reg, arbiter.LocalNodeFeatures())
	}
}
```

Create `dataplane/evidence/handler.go`:

```go
// Package evidence is the replay and byte-side scan path every verifying
// replica shares (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §8.1; plan S3-E1 contract §42.2):
// it replays a dispatched job through a replay core, scans the parts a scan
// request names, signs the scan with the replica's ed25519 evidence key and
// submits both to the arbiter's VerifierGateway. The network-pool verifier
// (package verifier) delegates to it byte for byte; the stage-3 member's
// verify role (member/consensus) runs it over its hg_member_unsafe replicas
// and its hg_rstage scratch. It also holds the replica's registration_seq
// and the signed VERIFIER registration both roles send.
package evidence

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"
	"google.golang.org/grpc"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/status"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// ReplayCore replays one job and returns the signed attestation.
type ReplayCore interface {
	Verify(ctx context.Context, job replay.ReplayJob) (replay.ReplayAttestation, error)
}

// Scanner recomputes the row LtHash of each named part.
type Scanner interface {
	Scan(ctx context.Context, parts []arbiter.PartRef) ([]arbiter.PartScan, error)
}

// Config names the replica: the id its evidence carries and the seed of the
// ed25519 key that signs its scans.
type Config struct {
	ReplicaID   string
	Ed25519Seed []byte
}

// Deps are the handler's collaborators.
type Deps struct {
	Client  *dataplane.Client
	Replay  ReplayCore
	Scanner Scanner
	// TablesReady gates a replay: it returns nil when the replica holds every
	// table the job needs, an error wrapping NotReady when it does not (the
	// job is refused and logged with NotReadyLog), and any other error when
	// its context ended (the job is refused unlogged). Nil accepts every job.
	TablesReady func(ctx context.Context, job replay.ReplayJob) error
	// NotReady is the sentinel TablesReady wraps; required with TablesReady.
	NotReady error
	// NotReadyLog is the warn message of a TablesReady refusal; empty is the
	// verifier's text.
	NotReadyLog string
	// Observe runs first for every replay job, before TablesReady and the
	// replay; an error refuses the job. Nil does nothing.
	Observe func(job replay.ReplayJob) error
	Logger  *slog.Logger
}

// verifierNotReadyLog is the network-pool verifier's add-gate refusal.
const verifierNotReadyLog = "table-set transition adds a table this verifier has not created; refusing to attest"

// Handler answers replay jobs and scan requests for one replica. It is safe
// for concurrent use when its collaborators are.
type Handler struct {
	cfg         Config
	d           Deps
	priv        ed25519.PrivateKey
	log         *slog.Logger
	notReadyLog string
}

// NewHandler validates cfg and d.
func NewHandler(cfg Config, d Deps) (*Handler, error) {
	if cfg.ReplicaID == "" {
		return nil, errors.New("evidence: replica id is required")
	}
	if len(cfg.Ed25519Seed) != ed25519.SeedSize {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("evidence: ed25519 seed must be %d bytes", ed25519.SeedSize)
	}
	if d.Client == nil || d.Replay == nil || d.Scanner == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("evidence: client, replay core, and scanner are required")
	}
	if d.TablesReady != nil && d.NotReady == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("evidence: TablesReady needs the NotReady sentinel it wraps")
	}
	log := d.Logger
	if log == nil {
		log = slog.Default()
	}
	notReadyLog := d.NotReadyLog
	if notReadyLog == "" {
		notReadyLog = verifierNotReadyLog
	}
	return &Handler{cfg: cfg, d: d, priv: ed25519.NewKeyFromSeed(cfg.Ed25519Seed), log: log, notReadyLog: notReadyLog}, nil
}

// HandleReplayJob observes the job, gates it on TablesReady, replays it and
// submits the attestation. It returns the first refusal; the arbiter
// re-dispatches an unattested job.
func (h *Handler) HandleReplayJob(ctx context.Context, m *pb.ReplayJob) error {
	job := wire.ReplayJobFromPB(m)
	if h.d.Observe != nil {
		if err := h.d.Observe(job); err != nil {
			h.log.Warn("evidence observer failed; refusing to attest", "block", m.GetBlockSeq(), "err", err)
			return err
		}
	}
	if h.d.TablesReady != nil {
		if err := h.d.TablesReady(ctx, job); err != nil {
			if !errors.Is(err, h.d.NotReady) {
				return err // the context ended while waiting
			}
			h.log.Warn(h.notReadyLog, "block", m.GetBlockSeq(), "err", err)
			return err
		}
	}
	att, err := h.d.Replay.Verify(ctx, job)
	if err != nil {
		h.log.Warn("replay verify failed; refusing to attest", "block", m.GetBlockSeq(), "err", err)
		return err
	}
	err = h.d.Client.WithLeaderRetry(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, conn *grpc.ClientConn) error {
		_, err := pb.NewVerifierGatewayClient(conn).SubmitAttestation(ctx, wire.AttestationToPB(att))
		return err
	})
	h.logSubmitFailure(ctx, "replay attestation", m.GetBlockSeq(), err, "receipt_hash", att.ReceiptHash)
	return err
}

// HandleScanRequest scans the requested parts, signs the scan and submits it.
func (h *Handler) HandleScanRequest(ctx context.Context, m *pb.ByteSideScanRequest) error {
	parts := wire.PartRefsFromPB(m.GetParts())
	scans, err := h.d.Scanner.Scan(ctx, parts)
	if err != nil {
		h.log.Warn("byte-side scan failed; refusing to attest", "block", m.GetBlockSeq(), "err", err)
		return err
	}
	msg := arbiter.ByteSideScanMsg{ReplicaID: h.cfg.ReplicaID, BlockSeq: m.GetBlockSeq(), Parts: scans}
	hash, err := replay.CanonicalDigest(arbiter.DomainByteSideScan, msg.Body())
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("scan hash: %w", err)
	}
	msg.ScanHash = hash
	msg.Signature = hex.EncodeToString(ed25519.Sign(h.priv, []byte(hash)))
	err = h.d.Client.WithLeaderRetry(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, conn *grpc.ClientConn) error {
		_, err := pb.NewVerifierGatewayClient(conn).SubmitByteSideScan(ctx, wire.ScanToPB(msg))
		return err
	})
	h.logSubmitFailure(ctx, "byte-side scan", m.GetBlockSeq(), err, "scan_hash", hash, "parts", len(scans))
	return err
}

// logSubmitFailure reports evidence the arbiter did not record. The gateway
// answers an FSM rejection (for example "scan_hash does not match the scan
// body") with InvalidArgument and logs nothing itself, and the subscription
// loop that called the handler only debug-logs its error, so without this
// line a deterministically rejected submission retries silently forever. It
// is observability only: nothing here feeds any hashed or signed data.
func (h *Handler) logSubmitFailure(ctx context.Context, kind string, blockSeq uint64, err error, attrs ...any) {
	if err == nil || ctx.Err() != nil {
		return
	}
	st, _ := status.FromError(err)
	args := append([]any{"kind", kind, "block", blockSeq, "replica", h.cfg.ReplicaID, "code", st.Code().String(), "err", err}, attrs...)
	h.log.Warn("arbiter did not accept verifier evidence", args...)
}
```

Create `dataplane/evidence/scanner.go`:

```go
package evidence

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"sort"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/chexec"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/ddl"
)

// CHScanner recomputes byte-side part commitments from the replicated tables
// of one database of the replica's ClickHouse: the verifier's hg_unsafe, a
// member's hg_member_unsafe.
type CHScanner struct {
	networkID string
	tables    []payloadexec.TableSchema
	database  string
	conn      clickhouse.Conn
	registry  dataplane.RegistryView
}

// NewCHScanner builds a scanner of database's tables. tables is the genesis
// table set; with a registry that is enabled, each table resolves through it
// (dataplane.RegistrySchema), and only while it is disabled (or nil) do the
// genesis tables apply.
func NewCHScanner(networkID string, tables []payloadexec.TableSchema, database string, conn clickhouse.Conn, registry dataplane.RegistryView) *CHScanner {
	return &CHScanner{networkID: networkID, tables: slices.Clone(tables), database: database, conn: conn, registry: registry}
}

// Database is the database the scanner reads.
func (s *CHScanner) Database() string { return s.database }

// Registry is the registry view the scanner follows; nil for none.
func (s *CHScanner) Registry() dataplane.RegistryView { return s.registry }

// Scan recomputes the row LtHash for every requested active part.
func (s *CHScanner) Scan(ctx context.Context, parts []arbiter.PartRef) ([]arbiter.PartScan, error) {
	byTable := map[string][]arbiter.PartRef{}
	tableOrder := []string{}
	for _, p := range parts {
		if p.PartName == "" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scan request part without a name (table %s partition %s)", p.TableID, p.PartitionID)
		}
		if _, ok := byTable[p.TableID]; !ok {
			tableOrder = append(tableOrder, p.TableID)
		}
		byTable[p.TableID] = append(byTable[p.TableID], p)
	}
	sort.Strings(tableOrder)

	out := make([]arbiter.PartScan, 0, len(parts))
	for _, tableID := range tableOrder {
		sch, err := s.SchemaFor(tableID)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		refs := byTable[tableID]
		names := make([]string, 0, len(refs))
		for _, p := range refs {
			names = append(names, p.PartName)
		}
		qualified := s.database + "." + ddl.CHTableName(tableID)
		results, err := chexec.ScanParts(ctx, s.conn, qualified, sch, names)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scan table %s: %w", tableID, err)
		}
		byName := map[string]chexec.PartScanResult{}
		for _, r := range results {
			byName[r.PartName] = r
		}
		for _, p := range refs {
			r, ok := byName[p.PartName]
			if !ok {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("part %s missing from scan results", p.PartName)
			}
			out = append(out, arbiter.PartScan{
				TableID:              p.TableID,
				PartitionID:          p.PartitionID,
				ClaimedPartRowLtHash: p.PartRowLtHash,
				ScannedPartRowLtHash: r.RowLtHash,
				LivePartName:         r.PartName,
			})
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

// SchemaFor resolves the table a scan names, by the SNode's rule. With an
// enabled registry the key's live incarnation decides
// (dataplane.RegistrySchema, shared with the SNode): a genesis-origin one uses
// the configured schema, a chain-origin one its registry schema_json verified
// against its schema_hash, so a same-name recreation of a retired genesis
// table is scanned with its new schema. Only while the registry is disabled
// (or not followed) do the configured genesis tables apply.
func (s *CHScanner) SchemaFor(tableID string) (payloadexec.TableSchema, error) {
	if s.registry != nil {
		if snap, enabled := s.registry.View(); enabled {
			return dataplane.RegistrySchema(s.networkID, s.tables, snap, tableID)
		}
	}
	for _, t := range s.tables {
		if t.TableID == tableID {
			return t, nil
		}
	}
	return payloadexec.TableSchema{}, fmt.Errorf("no schema configured for table %s", tableID)
}
```

```go
package evidence

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/snapshotquery"
)

// ReplayCoreConfig names the replica whose replay core NewReplayCore builds:
// its network, the id and ed25519 seed that sign its receipts, and the
// genesis table set.
type ReplayCoreConfig struct {
	NetworkID, ReplicaID string
	Ed25519Seed          []byte
	Tables               []payloadexec.TableSchema
}

// NewReplayCore assembles the real replay verifier over the materializer m:
// the verifier passes chexec.NewMaterializer (scratch in its connection's
// default database), a member chexec.NewMaterializerIn (scratch in hg_rstage
// under its prefix).
func NewReplayCore(cfg ReplayCoreConfig, m payloadexec.Materializer, manifests replay.SnapshotStore, payloads replay.PayloadStore) (*replay.Verifier, error) {
	signer, err := payloadexec.NewEd25519Signer(cfg.ReplicaID, cfg.Ed25519Seed)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("verifier signer: %w", err)
	}
	// NewDynamic: the configured tables are the genesis set; a table-set
	// transition job and the schemas a job carries extend it per job, so the
	// replay needs no registry access (dynamic SI table set, sub-project 2b).
	payload := payloadexec.NewDynamic(cfg.NetworkID, m, cfg.Tables...)
	// Query routes stay empty so the snapshot-query lane remains default-off.
	dispatcher, err := snapshotquery.NewCompositeExecutor(payload, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("verifier dispatcher: %w", err)
	}
	return &replay.Verifier{
		Snapshots:    manifests,
		Payloads:     payloads,
		Executor:     dispatcher,
		Signer:       signer,
		SchemaHashes: payloadexec.SchemaHashes{NetworkID: cfg.NetworkID, Tables: cfg.Tables},
	}, nil
}
```

Create `dataplane/evidence/registration.go`:

```go
package evidence

import (
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sync"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// RegistrationStateFile holds a verifying replica's last registration_seq,
// as {"registration_seq":N}: the verifier's only on-disk state, and a
// member's beside its install journal.
const RegistrationStateFile = "registration.json"

type registrationState struct {
	RegistrationSeq uint64 `json:"registration_seq"`
}

// RegistrationSeq reserves registration_seq values (housegate spec 2026-10-10
// §6.5). It is safe for concurrent use.
type RegistrationSeq struct {
	stateDir string
	mu       sync.Mutex
	last     uint64
}

// NewRegistrationSeq keeps the sequence in stateDir's RegistrationStateFile;
// an empty stateDir keeps it in memory, still clock-floored.
func NewRegistrationSeq(stateDir string) *RegistrationSeq {
	return &RegistrationSeq{stateDir: stateDir}
}

// Next reserves the registration_seq of the next Register call: max(last + 1,
// nowMillis), where last is the larger of this process's and the persisted
// value. With a state directory it is durable before it is returned
// (CONTRACT §3a); a lost file only drops the persisted floor.
func (r *RegistrationSeq) Next(nowMillis uint64) (uint64, error) {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	last := r.last
	if r.stateDir != "" {
		persisted, err := readRegistrationSeq(r.stateDir)
		if err != nil {
			return 0, err
		}
		last = max(last, persisted)
	}
	next := max(last+1, nowMillis)
	if r.stateDir != "" {
		if err := writeRegistrationSeq(r.stateDir, next); err != nil {
			return 0, err
		}
	}
	r.last = next
	return next, nil
}

func readRegistrationSeq(dir string) (uint64, error) {
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, RegistrationStateFile))
	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
		return 0, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("verifier registration state: %w", err)
	}
	var st registrationState
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &st); err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("verifier registration state corrupt: %w", err)
	}
	return st.RegistrationSeq, nil
}

// writeRegistrationSeq persists seq like the SNode's state.json
// (snode/state.go persistStateLocked): temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync.
func writeRegistrationSeq(dir string, seq uint64) error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o750); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("verifier state dir: %w", err)
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(registrationState{RegistrationSeq: seq})
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, ".registration-*")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = os.Remove(tmp.Name()) }()
	if _, err := tmp.Write(b); err != nil {
		_ = tmp.Close()
		return err
	}
	if err := tmp.Sync(); err != nil {
		_ = tmp.Close()
		return err
	}
	if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := os.Rename(tmp.Name(), filepath.Join(dir, RegistrationStateFile)); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	d, err := os.Open(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer d.Close()
	return d.Sync()
}

// VerifierRegistrationRequests builds the signed RegisterNode and MarkActive
// requests of one Register call of a VERIFIER-role node: both carry seq and
// are signed with priv, the key that signs the node's evidence, in ctx; the
// registration advertises arbiter.LocalNodeFeatures().
func VerifierRegistrationRequests(priv ed25519.PrivateKey, nodeID string, seq uint64, ctx authority.MessageContext) (*pb.NodeRegistration, *pb.NodeRef, error) {
	reg := wire.RegisterNode{Registration: arbiter.NodeRegistration{NodeID: nodeID,
		Roles: []arbiter.NodeRole{arbiter.NodeRoleVerifier}, Ed25519Pubkey: priv.Public().(ed25519.PublicKey), RegistrationSeq: seq}}
	var err error
	if reg.Ed25519Signature, err = authority.SignVerifierMessage(priv, authority.VerifierMessageRegistration, ctx, reg.Registration); err != nil {
		return nil, nil, err
	}
	mark := wire.MarkActive{NodeID: nodeID, RegistrationSeq: seq}
	if mark.Ed25519Signature, err = authority.SignVerifierMessage(priv, authority.VerifierMessageMarkActive, ctx,
		authority.MarkActiveBody{NodeID: mark.NodeID, RegistrationSeq: seq}); err != nil {
		return nil, nil, err
	}
	return wire.RegisterNodeToRequest(reg, arbiter.LocalNodeFeatures()), wire.MarkActiveToRequest(mark), nil
}
```

Replace the whole of `verifier/backends.go` with:

```go
package verifier

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/chexec"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/snapshotquery"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/evidence"
)

// NewReplayCore assembles the real replay verifier for this verifier role:
// evidence.NewReplayCore over chexec.NewMaterializer, whose scratch tables
// live in the connection's default database.
func NewReplayCore(cfg Config, conn clickhouse.Conn, manifests replay.SnapshotStore, payloads replay.PayloadStore) (*replay.Verifier, error) {
	return evidence.NewReplayCore(evidence.ReplayCoreConfig{
		NetworkID: cfg.NetworkID, ReplicaID: cfg.ReplicaID, Ed25519Seed: cfg.Ed25519Seed, Tables: cfg.Tables,
	}, chexec.NewMaterializer(cfg.NetworkID, conn), manifests, payloads)
}

// SnapshotQueryReplayCore adapts the query-only verifier to the role's
// dispatch port. Construction is explicit: callers that do not install a
// verified query route and historical policy leave the role default-off.
type SnapshotQueryReplayCore struct {
	verifier *snapshotquery.Verifier
}

// NewSnapshotQueryReplayCore installs no routes or authority itself. The
// caller must construct snapshotquery.Verifier with its immutable dispatcher,
// signer, and authenticated historical policy before injecting this core.
func NewSnapshotQueryReplayCore(v *snapshotquery.Verifier) (*SnapshotQueryReplayCore, error) {
	if v == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("snapshot query verifier is required")
	}
	return &SnapshotQueryReplayCore{verifier: v}, nil
}

// VerifySnapshotQuery forwards the exact trusted reference without deriving
// or normalising it. snapshotquery.Verifier owns the query-specific validation
// and receipt signing order.
func (c *SnapshotQueryReplayCore) VerifySnapshotQuery(ctx context.Context, job replay.SnapshotQueryJob, referenceID string) (replay.SnapshotQueryAttestation, error) {
	if c == nil || c.verifier == nil {
		return replay.SnapshotQueryAttestation{}, fmt.Errorf("snapshot query verifier is not configured")
	}
	return c.verifier.Verify(ctx, snapshotquery.VerifyRequest{Job: job, ReferenceID: referenceID})
}

// CHScanner recomputes byte-side part commitments from this verifier's
// ClickHouse: the evidence package's scanner over the verifier's hg_unsafe.
type CHScanner = evidence.CHScanner

// NewScanner builds a ClickHouse-backed byte-side scanner over the
// configured tables only.
func NewScanner(cfg Config, conn clickhouse.Conn) *CHScanner {
	return NewRegistryScanner(cfg, conn, nil)
}

// NewRegistryScanner builds a scanner that resolves tables through the table
// registry while it is enabled (nil registry: configured tables only).
func NewRegistryScanner(cfg Config, conn clickhouse.Conn, registry dataplane.RegistryView) *CHScanner {
	if cfg.UnsafeDatabase == "" {
		cfg.UnsafeDatabase = defaultUnsafeDatabase
	}
	return evidence.NewCHScanner(cfg.NetworkID, cfg.Tables, cfg.UnsafeDatabase, conn, registry)
}
```

```go
// chainIncarnation is dex.swaps (or another table of dex) as the registry
// records a chain-origin incarnation of it.
func chainIncarnation(t *testing.T, seq uint64, schema payloadexec.TableSchema, status wire.TableIncarnationStatus, scoped bool) wire.TableIncarnation {
	t.Helper()

		ScopedKeeperPath: scoped}
```
